-- shredded smoked tea duck  with ginger veg was DELICIOUS & without the hassle of all the bones ( I still did find a bone) Highly recommend this dish. The combination of smokey, gingery flavor was wonderful.

-- crust of cooked rice with pork. There were  fried rice cake wedges that came with the shredded/sauteed pork. I don't remember this dish being very hot but I really liked the rice cakes-pork combination although it was fairly oily.

--Dan Dan noodles were good. Less oily than at the other restaurants in Flushing but still oily and not as much flavor as the cold sesame noodles they make here. 

--fried potato in hot sauce - this was highly recommended here on Yelp, but the dish turned out to be crinkle cut french fries covered with szechuan pepper flakes. It's a good excuse for numbing your entire intestinal tract beginning with your lips and moving downwards.  For spice fanatics it's a must have dish but you could easily make this at home with frozen crinkle cut french fries sauteed in an 8 oz jar of szechuan pepercorns.  There wasn't much flavor except for hot and then numb. I would add onion, garlic & ginger.

--Braised sliced fish in spicy soup base. This was excellent. I didn't quite know what to expect but the Yelp reviews were all good and the waitress highly recommended it. It's served in a big black pot.  The broth is red and oily. The texture of the fish is similar to Tofu but it is boiled fish that melts in your mouth.  It is VERY spicy and I could only eat a little at a time with rice but it was delicious.  I took the remainder home and it was still good reheated several times.

I tried more dishes but am out of space.

Food was great and spicy. If you like spicy food and would like to try some authentic chinese food(not chinese takeout), this is a must. Its been a few months since my visit, so I don't remember what I ordered. But the noodles, meat, and rice were simply great.

Yes!!!! Cucumbers w/ supercharged garlic, scallion pancakes that are fried crispy without being greasy, dumplings in hot sauce (just the right amount of sweet in the chili oil), szechuan beef noodle soup (above average version). All for $25.60ish. Also great service. 

Balanced spicy- really lights up the flavor without burning your face off to the point you can't taste anything anyways.

The only thing that makes a trip to Target (just down the street) bearable.

It has become my favorite Sichuan spots ever!!! When i go in i don't even look at the menu, I ask the owner which is the guy usually behind the bar answer phones for his recommendations. I've been there a couple times and both times were very good. You can tell the dishes are very authentic because the owner himself is very passionate about the food. 

We ordered the hot fish casserole, dan dan mein, cold noodles, chicken in sichuan style and some other dishes i forgot the names too. But all recommended by the owner. Every single dish had their own characteristics and level of spice. The taste buds on my tongue was just outright loving it. 

I will be going there whenever I need my Sichuan fix!

You pass many Szechuan style restaurants and basically think they are all mostly the same.  Maybe you just go to them depending on the health grade.  However, you always order the same thing.  Well if that's you, Little Pepper is different.  You wouldn't think some restaurant along a strip of so-so to even questionable places would be any good.  But it is! No hacky stuff to get you in the door or make you get some special.  The staff is very nice (yes, English is not their strong suit but they are very nice).  SO what have I gotten here... shredded pork with spicy pepper (big time winner!) Minced beef with spicy noodles (incredible), steamed dumplings, wonton soup and of course the usual seasame chicken, general tso, type of stuff.  I'm not very versed in Asian cuisine but please trust me that this place is so different (in a very good way) then your regular old Szechuan place.
Follow the recommendations from yelp and you cant go wrong! Definitely the best szechuan in NYC!

Nice place to have a sit down lunch in college point.
Most of the Chinese restaurants on College Point Blvd.  are dives, but not this one.
Good food, clean, and cheap...

My absolute favorite Chinese restaurant, hands down, not a close second. Been eating and exploring Flushing for the better part of the past decade. What you trade off going a couple of miles north of Main Street is the neighborhood.  Less food and shopping options.  What you get in return is spot on amazing Szechuan cuisine.  I love the family that runs the restaurant. Few things make me happier than supporting a wonderful family that dedicate their lives to bringing the best of their culture to their customers. 

Ok..on to the food. Must haves..

Dry sautéed string beans
fresh cucumber with mashed garlic ...very strong garlic. 
Dumplings in Hot Oil...holy moly, the hot oil sauce is simply perfect. 
Chicken with peanuts...not the flavorless mess that passes for Kung Po Chicken on Long Island. A bit gingery, but I love ginger.
Tea Smoked Duck with ginger. No bones, fresh ginger and peppers,  this tastes like duck that was smoked. Absolutely spectacular

I once came in for lunch and had the Chendu (spelling?) Chicken. It was small delicious fried boneless pieces of chicken in a minefield of chilies and Szechuan peppercorns. Wow..numbing and spicy and I'm pissed that I didn't take home the leftover chilies to make a roasted chili oil.  

I remember driving 45 minutes for Chinese food with my parents when I was really young. I'm doing the same thing now with my kids, paying it forward to the next generation, exposing them to the best of the best.

One last thing..they are closed on Thursdays and don't take credit cards.  Cash Only. I spent $75 for dinner for 4 with a ton of leftovers.  Worth every penny
It's the best Sichuan food experience in New York. Every dish is just beautifully spicy, I love it!

As a true foodie who loves spicy Chinese food, Little Pepper has become my favorite place for Asian food. 
I discovered this place through Yelp. I was meeting with a contractor and it was lunchtime. College Point is the last place I'd expect a good meal; in the past, I could find decent pizza but little else there. Then I found rave reviews for Little Pepper and it's been a love affair ever since.
The food is nicely spiced but not crazy hot
and the cold sesame noodles, chicken with bamboo shoots (the shoots cut into long, lengthwise strands) , twice cooked pork, and eggplant in garlic sauce have been terrific.
The place actually has ambience and reasonably good service. As much as I like Spicy and Tasty in Flushing and the Yummy House in Elmhurst, this is my new fav.

Almost everything is spicy here.  Favorite dishes are the braised sliced fish and the spicy cold noodles.  Mapo Tofu is pretty simple and standard here as well.  I wasn't a fan of the meat balls but everyone else seemed to like it.

I'm usually not a fan of Szechuan. Mainly because it's 90% all spicy. But, I can never say no to venturing off to new places. Went with a couple of friends and thought this place wasn't too bad. It's out of the reach from the congested areas of flushing which was a plus! The food was great. Had all types of spicy flavors from sweet, to savory, to sour. I recommend the braised slice fish and their pork chicken meat balls. Their mapo Tofu was also good with rice! I would say this would definitely be a spot to hit during chilly nights! I dropped one star mainly cause I'm not THAT of a spicy eater. But that's just my own preference. This goes out for all the hot eaters out there! Oh and be patient with the waiters. Most of them don't really speak English. Point and order is the way to go!

Best sichuan food in NYC! They have food secretly made hot sauce! Amazing!
我们的好朋友老赵在这里找回了自己！
Awwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwwoooosome!

This is really a great restaurant! I had a wonderful dinner with friends. Authentic Szechuan food and secret spicy oil! Best Szechuan food I have ever had. Good and fast Service. They also have a nice place! Will come here again!
It's absolutely a great place to enjoy delicious spicy food with ur friends or family. 我们的好朋友老赵在这里找到了自己！

Little Pepper has the most authentic Szechuan food I have ever had in NYC, even throughout the US. Being spicy is one well-known feature of Szechuan food, but definitely not the whole story. Lettle Pepper preserves the rich tradition and essence flavor of Szechuan food. Taste it and feel it, you'll understand what "authentic" means.

I feel like I'm in bizzaro world or something.  4.5 stars with about 100 reviews.  recommended as one of the better Chinese restaurants in queens.  I really thought it was guaranteed that this would at the very least be a solid meal, but this was probably the worst meal I've ever had at a restaurant.

everything was incredibly salty.  border line inedible salty.  like accidentally mistaken 1 cup of salt for 1 tablespoon of salt salty.  I would have said that maybe perhaps the chef messed up 1 or 2 dishes, but 7/8 of our dishes were at that salt level and the only reason the 8th wasn't was because it was in a sweet sauce.

i love well seasoned and heavily spiced food.  I even like slightly over seasoned and over spiced food, so I consider myself very tolerant of strong flavors.  so when I say everything was stupidly salty,  it was really really freaken salty.

the cumin lamb was shocking.  did they literally just coat pieces of lamb in a thick crust of cumin powder and cook it?  is that food?  y not save time and just directly eat spoonfuls of cumin powder?  I also thought to myself, even if the seasoning was toned down, the lamb and duck we got were dry and chewy anyway.  the pork belly was harmless and completely forgettable.   the cold noodles were, ummm, tasted like left overs then thrown together with pantry ingredients.  mapo tofu was, outside of the brine sauce it was sitting in, bland and one dimensional.  I can't even comment on the dandan noodles because the salt from the sauce is still lingering in my mouth a day later.   I did enjoy the dumplings.  those were great.  perfectly chewy in a nice sweet sauce.  and they did cook all the noodles properly.  also, the fish dish we got was solid.  the fish was meltingly tender and edible when taken out of the salty sauce and eaten with rice.

I truly hope the chef was just extremely off that night because if the food I ate is the food that earned all this praise, I may just have to move to a different planet.  I cannot begin to comprehend how what was served to me is acceptable let alone earn any type of accolade.  I wouldn't serve this food to my dog.   but again, it wasn't even the salt.  everything felt amateurish and one dimensional.  it tasted like the food of a mom who's bad at cooking but doesn't know she's bad at cooking.

I come to Little Pepper at least once a month. This place is ridiculously good  I love Sichuan food and this place has the best Sichuan food in New York. Their double cooked fish, mapo tofu, and beef with spicy green peppers are what I order each time I come to this restaurant. If you have never eaten at Little Pepper, you have never tried good sichuan food :)

My girlfriend from Zhejiang, China and I found this place walking down College Point Blvd. and now make it a regular stop. The best Chinese Sichuan restaurant in the Flushing area as far as we're concerned. I really like their Gong Bao Ji Ding...aka Kung Pao Chicken

Visited after reading review in NY Magazine's Cheap eats. I have to echo Donnie D's comment. The restauarnt was very clean and the staff friendly and attentive. However, the dished we had were close to inedible by virtue of the saltiness. Salt was the overwhelming flavor which is a shame because the dishes were cooked perfectly and the ingredients fresh,
Good food but very very very very very bad service, the old lady never been happy. 如果那个老女人炒鱿鱼了就回去吃。
I Love your food， but the the service is sooooooooooo Sick， I mean the server woman is sick, she should get fire.

I cannot stop thinking about their cold noodles! 
It was the best thing I ate that evening. Vinegary with just the right amount of spiciness.  

In hindsight we should have ordered something to balance the spiciness of the dishes. All our dishes were so spicy. It was delicious.
Average - nothing special - just don't order fish dish, looks like the oil and ths soup was reused

The best Sizchuan food in NYC - just the best and no close runner up!  Dan Dan noodle, double cooked pork, whole fish in minced pork, ox tongues in chili sauces, beans with minced pork.  All these dishes are phenomenal and one level higher than those peers in other restaurants.  I have been there multiple times and never find it disappointing.  If i want spicy food, this is my go to place.  

The price is affordable and easy to park.  But this place is not walkable from flushing subway, which could be good, as it keeps the restaurant less crowed and cheaper.

The food is good and spicy, like a real Szechuan food. But I was wait over 20 mins to get my food, too long. They don't have many people dine in at 1:00 pm . The waiter just kept saying the food will be ready soon, it's ridiculous.

This is the BEST Szechuan I've had in NYC! Very nice service too.The sliced fish in spicy broth is unreal - the most amazing combination of spices, veggies, spicy oil, and fresh cilantro on top! Stir fried dry string beans are the best I've had. I wish I lived closer...

When to LittlePpepper for dinner on 9/27/14.  Made reservation for 7:30pm  for a party of 9. We got there around 7:20 pm Restaurant did n't honor our Rev.  give our table away.  Parking on Sat night is terrible .  We were seated  Not thing was set up plates ,glass wares, chop sticks tea cups. and naps.  The waiter brought the setting  and we had to pass it  around.  After we place ours setting down we notice  the table was oily and disgusting.  We ask the waiter to clean the table .  He give us a look. We pick up our setting and he clean the table .  Looking at the  menu .  We ask waiter what type of fresh fish listed on the  menu .  He said "I don't know", We ask time X3  He stood there kept saying I don't know. He is lazy or just dumb.  So we decided to order the fish with crisp rice anyway .  Now we ask him what is crisp rice he said I don't and walk away .  Other waiter came to take our order we ask him what is crisp rice He didn't either and try to show us with his hands and shaking his head. First waiter dumb ,2nd waiter dumber.  The pancake was good and fresh fish w/ crisp rice was fair. slow to come out. from the kitchen. All the other 9 dish was too spice ( over pepper) . Some of us like chili but this is crazy, The 2 order the  DAN Dan noodle was was very very salty and  we was not able to eat it.  We should of sent it back, but we didn't. The cold water was excellent .  Go if you like beyond vey poor service and poor food.

Read the review and come here, the food is not bad, but heavy oil like most chinese food. I don't have any complain about the food. But the service is really bad, the waiter doesn't know what he is doing. Just waste my time waiting there around 20 minutes to be seated. And the customers love to talk very loud, which is very unpleasant, anyway I will not come here again, also the neighborhood doesn't look friendly. I am afraid to get robbed anytime...

Best Szechuan food I ever eat! DanDan noodle got both a cute name and the good taste! I also order the fish in hot soup, that dish just made my day really, we put the spicy soup on rice and it is too good to be true! I definitely will introduce my friend in NYC to come to little pepper, love all the dishes we order today! FYI 3 ppl 5 dishes and only 65 plus tax!

So the food was good but the service left something to be desired.   The server got our order wrong and then the other server didn't even look at us when we were given the check! There was a large party that was going on but I'm not convinced they were unable to handle the flow.   Ouch!

The stars say it all.   Enjoyed everything cant wait to come back and explore more items on the menu.  From the first taste of food (pork belly appetizer btw) I knew the kitchen was run by someone who cared about the food and knew what he was doing.
Also parking is easy at least during the weekday afternoon we were there.  Prices were reasonable and the decor was simple and clean with a lot of very enjoyable artwork done by the owner/chef's son which added to the overall experience.  Again, I have to say you should come here if you want good, authentic Szechuan that is so delicious with a lot of complex flavors that include the spicy you would expect but also hints of sweet, savory and tangy.  Definitely the best sichuan ive ever had.  Ever!!

We got take out from here today. Surprise! It was delicious. It was a bit tough to communicate our order since the English is very limited. We ordered 2 lunch specials and they come with soup and rice. We asked for wonton and hot & sour soup. Instead of telling us the lunch specials come with egg drop soup only, we were charged an extra $8 for soup. When we complained, the gentleman acted like he didn't understand us. The food however, was delish. We will go again, but be more careful when placing orders.

I came from Chengdu, I love the food here! Everything I taste tonight just bring me back to my hometown! 口水鸡，夫妻肺片，干锅，辣子鸡什么都有，甚至还有担担面！！老板会说四川话,哈哈
You can find everything famous in Sichuan province with authentic taste here. If you want to try spicy Chinese food, come to visit this restaurant in flushing! You'll get surprise here:)

I'm a HUGE fan of of Szechuan food and I love to go to Flushing to revel in that burnt-mouth feeling as often as I can manage. There are a lot of good places to eat, but I think this one has become my favorite. 

The decor is super basic and the service is definitely more family-style than professional, but it's all about the food. I haven't tried the US-style dishes so much, so I can't speak to the General Tso's, but some of my favorite dishes include:

Sichuan Style Double Cooked Pork  (notice: the pork is cut more like bacon)
Braised Sliced Fish In Spicy Soup Base
Cumin Lamb
Shredded Potato with green pepper
Sauteed Snow Pea Leaves 
Dandan Noodle
Dumplings in red oil

If you're a fan of the cuisine, it's definitely worth a trip out there.

love love this place!

I always order the braised slice fish and the spicy cold noodles.  I believe the price for the fish dish went up by $1. It used to be $14.95 and now it's $15.95 The beef tendons was also delish. The mapo tofu was good but it could be a little bit spicer. Skip anything thats not hot and spicy. I've ordered the Chicken with mixed vegetables and boy was that a failed. It tasted like a dish from a regular chinese take out resturant.

Terrible Service, Won't go back again.

Three of us went here for lunch today.  During our one hour visit, we were the only 3 in the entire restaurant.  You would think that the one waiter there could have handled it, even if he did not speak one word of English.   We each ordered a soup and  a  lunch special. After a 10 minute wait we had to interupt the waiter watching the TV and ask for a second pot of tea (in sign language).    Each food item came out at a different time.   First, my shredded beef and peppers came out.  After waiting for about 5 more minutes we just put the plate in the middle of the table and shared it.  Then a second lunch of shrimp and vegetables came out.  5 minutes later, one of the soups.  5 minutes after that the other 2 soups. Finally the last general tso's lunch arrived. We needed to call the waiter away from the TV 3 more times for napkins, soy sauce and the check.  The food was tasty but overwhelmed by the rude service and small size portions.  In conclusion, if you are hungry,  don't speak Chinese, want to eat at the same time as the rest of the people at your table and expect normal restaurant service ,pass on Little Pepper.

What a nice birthday lunch at Little Pepper today! So glad choose Little Pepper over Joe s Shanghai.  Two year ago was here once took out a whole fish dish of theirs.  Impressed again today.  Will definitely go back to try other fish dishes soon.  The service is kind plain. But  I can put up with that since the fish is extraordinary. Or simply avoid eating in, order take out.  Prices are few dollars more than other similar restaurant in Flushing such as Spicy and Tasty.

Very good food. The flavors were very authenticate. The Dan Dan noodle and the chicken cold dish were the best I have tasted so far. Really delicious, just a bit oily to my taste. I strongly recommend this place!

I really like this place! My friend suggested it for our gathering and being a fan of spicy foods, I said ok! It's a family style type of place. We ordered 4 things: dumplings, sautéed dried string beans, spicy squid dish, and beef cumin dish. The beef dish is the spiciest of the 4 and delicious. It was quite tender despite looking burnt. The squid was also yummy in its thick and somewhat clear sauce. I thought it had bamboo from the looks, but it turned out to be mushrooms (Don't blame me, it wasn't the usual white mushrooms. You would think they were bamboo shoots, too). The string beans were also strangely addicting. I'm normally not a string beans fan but I found myself picking them up quite often. The dumplings, on the other hand, was a miss for me. It was kind of sweet and I'm not a fan of sweet meat dumplings but to each their own because my friends liked it. The place is not crowded (at least not when I went) so that's nice. The only bad thing is that the neighborhood seems a tad bit sketchy at night. For the awesome, spicy and delicious dishes though...I definitely see myself coming back for more!

Sweet, spicy, salty, and did I mention SPICY?

I want to eat it all. It's rare that in NYC I will go back to a restaurant repeatedly, but Little Pepper makes the cut. And this restaurant is deep in Queens, not necessarily the most friendly public transportation wise area if you are coming from other boroughs or Western Queens. It's worth the trek. I carpool. I'd even stick out my thumb for this one.

I've watched Little Pepper grow and change over the years. What was once divey, is now a really nice Sichuan restaurant complete with newly revamped menus (laminated and all). The portions have shrunk but it is the quality that matters. On a good day, with a good chef, you'd be eating in tears and sweats. The spice and taste is that good, that hot, and that satisfying. You'll eat till you are stuffed to the brim if you're anything like me and let gluttony get the best of you.

This place is a million times better than Han Dynasty. If you're clueless as to what to order, bring your Mandarin speaking friends or just follow this cheat cheat:

Dan dan noodles (2 orders)
Sliced Pork Belly with chili garlic sauce
Prawns with chili pepper
Sliced fish with bean curd
Mapo Tofu
Braised Fish in spicy soup base
Sichuan style double cooked pork
Shredded Pork w/bamboo shoots
Minced Pork with clear noodle
Dried Sauteed String Beans
Lotus Root with dried pepper sichuan style
Spicy cold noodle
Dumpling in hot sauce

Yes, I ate all of this. I am a champion. They even have dessert. I wouldn't advise on ordering it though because they seemed annoyed when we did. But if you really really love rice dumplings then I suppose you can force them to boil some out of the freezer.

Stick to the entrees and bring your appetite. It's no fun to come here with people who don't eat.

Had water cooked fish,mapatofu and spicy chicken w peppers and sesame. Spicy chicken had too much sesame seeds and they use those minty sour Chinese spice to make the flavor, so if you are not a fan of that numb tongue feeling I dont recommend.
Mapatofu is really good, so soft and sauce is delicious. Water cooked fish is my favorite. very soft and just right amount of spice.

This place is unreal. The food is so authentic and delicious, I literally crave eating here. We had so many delicious things, my mouth is watering just thinking about it. The cumin lamb is a must, chili shrimps delicious and a huge portion, dan dan noodles are also delicious they are different than I've had them at other Szechuan places but I liked them a lot. The rabbit is really tender and cooked to perfection. The vegetables sides were on point, we got the snowpea shoots which I could have eaten an entire plate myself they were so delicious. I will absolutely come back here again, one of my new favorite spots in Queens. Left with my mouth burning in the best kind of way. My new favorite Szechuan spot :)

What the f I just picked up my lunch special and it says it comes with rice and soup so I asked for pork fried rice and hot and sour soup. I end up getting white rice and they charged me for the soup saying hot and sour soup is not conplimentary.. So why advertise saying soups included?

I love this place, it makes my nose run and my eyes water.  It's HOT. It's strong.  Its Szechuan.  Its a big menu, normally not a good idea. Today's chefs take 10 entrees and make sure they're all kick-ass, and change things with the season.  The old school is to offer 55 things, have something for everybody and watch food costs sink the profits. 
   I like lamb. I don't find enough lamb out there. So that's what I eat here.  That and the tripe.  I think I just killed my Yelp legitimacy.  I like exotic, what can I say.  I like being the only caucasian American in a restaurant.  
    I really like Szechuan, that Chinese people eat.....And I hate "Chinese Take-Out", that's not even a little bit Chinese. Its Koreans in the back working a deep fryer.  The Sweet and Sour chicken is just chicken nuggets with some red sauce made of high fructose corn syrup that came from a bottle. Its as Chinese as KFC and Big Macs. It's fast food thats supposed to be exotic because there's sugar, salt and fat...So...its pretty much McDonalds  with some soy sauce on the side.

Food was decent but when I try to order over the phone for take out, they can't understand. Tried ordering with the number, I.E. L1 or P14, and they couldn't understand that either. Tried with the name and nothing. Maybe get at least one person that can speak even just a little English.

I've only been here twice, both for family occasions, both when we were 1 of 2 large parties, and both meals were delicious. 

This unassuming restaurant seems almost out of place on College Point Blvd where the best Chinese food you'd expect is your run of the mill take out joint. Even if some of my good opinion of this place is a product of its environment aka lackluster dining competition, all I know is:

- The food is delicious and your taste buds will benefit most if you order a nice assortment of cold and hot meat and veggie dishes.
- They've got a pretty neat collection of paintings that isn't limited to the usual Chinese art, which makes the place slightly more contemporary/cool than other joints.
- I love how the chef comes out to greet all parties, asks how everything is, and bids us farewell. It's clear he takes pride in the food he cooks all guests.

Actually it would be 3.5 stars but as the 1/2 star doesn't exist I had to choose for 3 this time.
I liked very much the fact that the place is clean and there are all this nice modern paintings on the wall.
The service is nice enough, but their english is not the best so I suggest that you go there with your clear ideas of what you want to eat, without many questions to ask...

We ordered 5 dishes for the two of us. We finished everything as usual. Perfect timing because the street parking allows max 1hour so we didn't have to go out and add extra time/money...

It was not busy, today, sunny Saturday of the Memorial Day long weekend, around 12.30 pm

Overall our meal was Ok+, even though everything was very salty and with that spicy canola oil taste. All dishes were spicy, but not impossible to eat. And not too hot, which today for me was ok, but in general I would prefer all dishes coming out "smoking".

- Salt/pepper shrimps: no head, not much flavor, crunchy and a bit greasy. I have had these similar shrimps in many chinese restaurants in Italy, nothing special. Most probably frozen stuff. 

- Dan Dan Noodles: salty, but I liked the consistency and the flavor

- Spicy fried long beans: nice but extremely salty

- Wontons in Chili oil: an interesting mix of sweet and spicy taste, nice enough but not too juicy and so difficult to catch with those plastic chopsticks! I wanted to ask for a fork...

- Cumin Lamb: very simple, very Cumin flavored, not well balanced

Clearly we couldn't see a twist on this meal, everything was nice but had some mistakes to our taste

Total $53 = tip
Bathroom is clean

This has been on my hit list for quite some time and after a long night of watching the Rangers lose I was craving spicy food. The food was as follows: braised sliced fish in spicy soup. It was some of the best I have had in NYC. It was spicy but not so powerful that you lost the flavors and overpower the fish. There was not as much cabbage as I have had elsewhere but there was a nice addition of mushrooms. The wontons in spicy sauce was nice but not as spicy as I prefer. We also had another order of wontons in a sweeter soy sauce. The wontons are made from a nice thin pasta with a nice pork stuffing. The vegetable was the fried green beans which were amazing. I will be back and try other things on this menu.

1 star for rude service.

Called in on a Sunday night around 8pm, ordered 3 dishes and told them I would be there 30mins later.  Once arrived I spoken to a lady behind the counter, stating the orders I have made, she looked at me confused and said( What you picked up already ) I said No No, I called in 30mins and said I will be there soon. Then she ask the waiters and turned out my order was placed under the menu books and it was NEVER given in to the kitchen. 

I then ask ok, so how long if I order now? She replied with a rude tone LOOK WE ARE BUSY, IF YOU CANT WAIT THEN DONT ORDER. 

I was like excuse me, YOU messed up and don't take it out on paying customer.  I walked out and promise myself NEVERTHELESS to come back here again!!

Their food is a welcome addition to the area. The food is better than any Chinese food place in the area, no contest. It's restaurant quality food for a great price. It's the the best I've had in Queens. The only issue this place has is no one speaks English and it's impossible to place a order of the phone. If the hire someone who speaks English it's a five star place. Service was fast and everyone was pleasant. I can't wait to go back.

They have really good food, if you're into spicy food. It's like a sweet kind of spicy, which I like, and I'm not used to eating spicy food at all. Never grew up eating spicy food. Its a small place with limited seating, but they always find a way to accommodate everyone. Reasonable prices too...

I love the food.   We ordered Chong Qing chicken, plain broth beef noodle soup, eggplant in soy sauce, and stirred fried greens.  I enjoyed the food because each dish has its distinctive favor, and prepared in a way that is close to home cooking.
Great little gem to have a nice cooked meal. Dishes were simple and flavorful. Good service and clean

Authentic cuisine and amazingly spicy, need I say more?! Szcheuwan chicken was made perfectly and the chicken with broccoli was fresh and light compared to regular chienese take-out. Glad to have discovered this on my late night yelp hunt for food! Definitely a must try :)

I'd say it's 3.5.
food is alright, decent szechuan food since my friend from szechuan is wiling to come back.
very quiet, easy to park, but I'm not super impressed.

Let me start the review by saying that this is one of my favorite Sichuan restaurants.  It is a bit out of the way and not easy to get to if you don't have a car.  The restaurant is in College Point, which is another 10-15 minute drive from downtown Flushing.  It has a small store front in a nondescript block, but trust me, the food in there is kind of amazing, and well priced.  After a few visits, I've finally decided to write a review about the place.  The dishes I've described below are the ones I've tried at the most recent visit as they are still fresh on my mind.  See below for details.

Cumin Lamb - my favorite dish here.  I love how tender and flavorful the meat is, and the lamb is cooked to perfection.  I always order this dish whenever we come here.  It could be a bit "game-y" for those who have not tried lamb before, but it is definitely worth a try as you may discover your new favorite protein.

Whole Fish in Bean Sauce - second favorite dish.  I hate cooking fish at home, so I always try to order them when I go to a restaurant.  I particularly love whole fish prepared in a kick-ass sauce.  Little Pepper's sauce is sweet and sour, with a trace amount of spiciness.  I love the fact that the fish is reasonably priced here (I think it is around $20 here) and the price is actually listed on the menu.  Most Chinese places usually list the whole fish price as "mp" and try to elevate the price to astronomical amounts when you order it.

Dried Sauteed String Bean - another great dish.  I can never replicate string beans as the way they make it here.  It is such a simple dish, but I love how the string beans are crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, and perfectly seasoned.  

Dan Dan Noodles - this is the guy's favorite dish.  I think it is a tad to spicy for my taste, but I do appreciate how well the noodles are cooked, and that it is not too greasy as this dish tends to become in other Chinese restaurants

Szechuan Picked Vegetable - it is like Chinese kimchi, but more sour than spicy.  It is a good complement to the spicy dishes, and sort of like a palate cleanser between dishes.

Thin Sliced Beef Tendon with chili sauce - my least favorite dish.  I thought it was too spicy and the tendons were too mushy.

There are a couple of other dishes that I've tried in the past and really enjoyed, including the beef with peppers and shredded potatoes. It is a pretty authentic Sichuan restaurant, and as a result, some of the dishes could get quite spicy.  If you are not a big fan of spicy food, tell them to tone down the spiciness in advance.  I found them to be particular good about requests.  I always think that I can handle more spice than I am actually capable of, which is a false bravado that I need to address :)  Anyway, if you have a chance to stop by, you will thank me for it!

Wow. Amazing. This was several weeks ago. An experienced friend ordered for all of us and every dish was to die for. Duck, greens, dumpling in spicy oil, cold nest of noodles, cold spicy tofu. Can't remember everything. Couldn't stop eating, and I thought I was in relatively restrained mood before arriving.

Ok. Just a little background. I drove about 40 minutes to find this place, since I love Szechuan food and have been to about a dozen top rated Szechuan restaurants in New York and read many good things on the Internet about this place. I couldn't try everything so I'll cut right to the chase on those things I always order at these places. I ordered both types of dumplings that were on the menu, and expected at least one of them to be very spicy with a fiery pepper taste. No such luck, as one of the dishes was mildly spicy and the other one completely bland (I actually think they just screwed up the dish and forgot to add the peppers or spice). Then I ordered the dish that got me hooked on Szechuan food, three pepper chicken (I was able to order it in Chinese since I had ordered it dozens of times at the other places and memorized how to say it in Chinese). The waiter tells me they don't have that dish, and after speaking with what appeared to be the management staff I was finally able to order it. And yes, the dish was very good; however my only complaint was that is didn't have enough hua jiao (that's how it is said in Chinese) and it refers to a little pepper that makes the tongue a little numb but is very tasty. I was more than a little surprised by this, given that the name of the restuarant was Little Pepper! All in all, it appears to be a very adequate little quick stop for Szechuan food, but certainly not worth the long drive. If you want fresh and fiery Szechuan food, there are a few in downtown Flushing, and you won't have to search for them!

The food was perfectly fine, but it felt like they backed off the spice for white people. What should have been a nice spicy Szechuan meal turned into the same old bland boring Chinese food. Definitely not worth the trip.

I had dinner here tonight because I was nearby and turned help on. I found little pepper, there use to be a location on Roosevelt Ave in flushing and I thought I'd give it a try. I forget the names of the things I got but, it was garlic pork, hot and spicy beef pot, pork and rice crispy, Kung Pao chicken. 

The pork and garlic is s authentic schechuan dish and is usually pork belly thinly slicked with spicy sauce. Served cold, if anything warm. This dish came and the pork belly was perfectly sliced, warm and delicious. However it was a little too sweet for my liking. Schechuan food is sully almost never sweet.... That's more of a Cantonese and American thing. 

The kung Pao chicken was WAYY too sweet. This dish was starchy and good except for the sugar part. I would probably never order this again, or if I do if advise the chef in regards to the sweetness of the dish. 

The beef was good. It wasn't mouth watering good as the places in flushing but this was the best out of all the dishes. The spiciest is just right with the right amount of spices(numbing spice) and it's exactly how I'd make it. Delicious. 

Then came the pork with rice crackers. This is super Americanized because authentic Chinese food usually do not put chunks of carrot and snow pea and mushrooms in their dish. This was off and it was starchy, however the starchy sauce became watery very fast. Making the dish not so good after. I also asked for the (awfully delicious) rice crackers to be on the side because I didn't want it to be soggy when eating. Which, is the best idea ever. 

Overall, if I'm in the area again I would come here again, but I would ask the chef not to put any sugar in my dishes. I would also try other things in the restaurant if the chance ever comes up again.

Good Food... Excellent Customer Service 
My group had the general tso's chicken, sautéed dried beans, egg fried rice and fish in bean sauce. The sautéed dried beans had a kick to it, so avoid it if spicy food isn't your thing. Overall, the food was good, everyone was happy with their meal!

This place is a hidden gem in flushing! They have THE MOST AMAZING cumin beef! Their dumplings in spicy sauce is also really tasty. I've been here multiple times and they never disappoint. Staff is always friendly as well.

I absolutely love this place! I have found my replacement dan dan noodle spot! It is on the further side, but wirth the trek into college point. Beau and i had the dan dan noodles, szechuan style double cooked pork, and the dumplings in hot sauce. I would give them all a 100%! I can't wait to go back and try out the other menu items!

I went there with a few friends during a weekday for dinner, it was pretty quiet.  The food was delicious and can be spicy (the restaurant is call "Little Pepper).  We order the fish that came in a bowl full of hot oil, delicious but be careful if you can't take spicy food.  Dumpling was also great!  Overall, I had a nice experience and I will definitely be back!

The only food worth driving 50 mins, one way for(West Babylon to College Point). First off the dining area is extremely clean and well lit. Secondly the food is off the charts amazing, every time we come we try a new dish along with the standard list of favorites. Some must try favorites in no particular order; double cooked pork, minced pork with clear noodles, dumplings in hot sauce, cucumber with garlic and the scallion rice. We come here at least once every two weeks for our Szechuan fix.

Ooooooooohhh yea!!!! Long live peppers and spice!! So happy we found this place. Legit Sichuan food -Thank you Yelpers for steering me here!

All the classics are great - spicy fish, string beans, Dan Dan noodles - so good, cheap and authentic.

My co-worker and I ordered from this place recently. We ordered the Mapo tofu and Garlic pork with rice. The mapo tofu was TOO salty and the garlic pork was TOO sweet. Mind you, I eat all my meals mostly salty compared to most and if I am saying it is too much, it wasn't worth it. I ended up throwing my meal away after a few bites, lost my appetite that I worked up all morning. Although I like szechuan food, I am not ordering it for a while.

Mm... Szechuan so good. Prices are fantastic. Portions are kind of small. Or maybe we are just big eaters haha. Sometimes we just order an extra rice. The food is saucy and delicious. I really like the dandan noodles here. We frequent the chicken and broccoli. It's a little different I think there's some ginger in it. Changes up the flavor a little. I got the eggplant in garlic sauce the first time I went there..a little spicy. I really liked it tough! I did not like the egg drop soup here. Wouldn't get it again. Will come back again and again though and they still get five stars because everything else is so good and I'm picky with my soups

Cons
Service was not good. While very nice, they were understaffed, and not attentive to refill needs or extra napkins. It was hard to get attention because they were always moving quickly. It took us an hour to get our food once seated. Our waiter told us it was slow, so we weren't that upset, but an hour really is too long for a small casual restaurant. Last con- CASH ONLY. Credit cards should be standard now. 
We did go the weekend after a NYT review, so maybe they weren't prepared for the rush. 

Pros
Green tea when you are seated. Nice atmosphere. Nice workers. The food is REALLY GOOD. Except the rabbit, too many bones for me. The soups were fantastic, as was the general tsos. I probably won't come back if service doesn't change, but I'll definitely order takeout.

Four of us went because of the review in the Times. Packed but we'd made a reservation and had our table in just a few minutes. Service was pleasant but incredibly slow. Probably because of the others who were there because of the Times. It took an hour before our first dish arrived. However...after that, pure joy. Cucumbers with mashed garlic. Silken tofu with scallions. Tea smoked duck. Cumin lamb. Dan Dan noodles. And on and on. Most exciting food in ages!!!
It's a salt land!! Everything is extremely salty with a lot of MSG!!! My friends and I have MSG reaction after eating the dinner there. If there was minus stars, I would give -5.

Came here for a birthday dinner. Service was ok. The spiciness of the food is good and recommended if you enjoy hot food. BUT unfortunalety all the dishes we ordered about 10 different ones were extremely salty and they used a lot of MSG.

We chose this place for a friend's birthday dinner based on a good review on NY Times, but was really disappointed. The food was way too salty. For certain dishes, like the popular spicy beef tendons and arctic clams with wasabi, you could actually taste grains of undissolved salt and MSG with each bite. And also, the service was slow and inattentive. We will not be returning.

Cash only! 

This is one of my favorite szechuan restaurants in the city. I honestly haven't been able to find a good authentic Chinese restaurant since I moved to NY from Chicago...until now! Came here with a group of 5 and loved the food. Would recommend the cumin lamb, ChongQing chicken, Dan Dan noodles, Fish with ground pork, and sautéed string beans with pickled mustard greens. 

Only thing is it is a pretty far off the beaten path (East of laguardia airport) so would recommend taking an uber or lyft from Flushing. Hailing a car on the way back was much more difficult. Also not sure if this was because they just had a health inspection a couple of weeks ago but it was one of the cleanest Chinese restaurants I've ever been to.

Wowza.

Order rice at the beginning. All the dishes pair so well with rice.

Recs:
Dan Dan noodles - tasty, tender noodles and deliciously spicy.
Scallion fried rice - so surprisingly simple and so good. Rice just tastes like scallions and oil
Cumin lamb - Really, good and incredibly spicy. 
Chongqing Chicken 
Fish with ground pork

It's worth a trip out to College Point. Probably the best Szechuan food we've had in NYC.

One of the best authentic Szechuan restaurants in  Queens. Their English is pretty limited, so you may have to point. The Dan Dan noodles and dumplings were awesome. String beans were a little too salty, but still tasty. Some things can get pretty spicy since they aren't shy about using their chilies. Different cuisines have different types of spicy, and you know it's Szechuan spicy when your tongue has a slight metallic taste/touch to it, which I guess is unique to the chili peppers used.

Probably the best Szechuan restaurant I've been to in New York, or anywhere in the U.S. for that matter. Really, really delicious and a very good deal. Would recommend the Mapo Tofu, Dried Sauteed String Beans, Dumpling in Hot Sauce, and Dandan Noodle. All really awesome.

Came here after an afternoon at SpaCastle with my two kids.  We ordered the spicy beef tendon, dan dan noodles, mapo tofu, and dumplings in hot chili oil.  The food was delicious and the kids were happy. We all love a little spice.

I will say that the tofu was flavored well and cooked nicely.  The beef tendon was good and we couldn't stop picking at it.  The dan dan noodles and dumplings were spicy, but not as spicy as expected.  In fact, there was a little sweetness behind the spice.  We didn't mind it, but if you were expecting traditional scheczuan spice, you would be dissapointed.

The place was clean and the service was quick and friendly.

Great Food with just the right amount of heat in every dish.
The prices are very, very reasonable.
I wish there was one in Nassau County.
Lamb, Tofu, Scallion Fried Rice, Scallion Pancake, Dumplings, Chicken, DanDan Noodle, Fish, Eggplant, Duck all Fantastic.....

Ate here tonight with two friends. Two of us were veg and the third was non-veg. 
We ordered numerous items and all of them tasted great. 
App: scallion pancake, which was delicious and the sauce was amaze. Veg. 
Dumpling in Hot Sauce- scrumptious. Perfect amount of spice and the dumplings were light and delicate. Not veg. 
Dried Sautéed String Beans- a perfect combo of salty and spicy. Veg.

Came here upon the recommendation of a friend who saw the NYT review. What a great experience. 

Little Pepper is located in College Point. Now I went to grade school in College Point and never in a million years would I think that a restaurant like this would be here. It was a fantastic surprise.

The restaurant is fairly small comprising of just one medium sized room. There are a healthy number of tables for parties of all sizes (eg: four people, eight people, two people, etc). Table tops are glass, and for good reason; things can get messy--in the best way!

We enjoyed a number of dishes: thin sliced beef tendon, dan dan noodles, shredded pork in garlic sauce, and lamb (heavy on the cumin). Of all the dishes, the shredded pork in garlic sauce was by far my favorite. Everything was unbelievably flavorful, but this was out of this world. Everyone in the party had different favorites so in short, they are all winners.

For drinks, you can enjoy wine or beer. The beer is incredibly reasonable. We're talking $2.50 for a Bud and $3.50 for something better. You'll want a couple as things can get hot. And while we're talking about hot, this food can get hot not, but it was not not on this occasion. Our guess is that the kitchen toned it down for us, but I'm not complaining. The food was well seasoned and spicy to enjoy, not so hot that it couldn't be consumed.

I can safely say that i'll be going out of my way to return to Little Pepper to enjoy more of what their menu has to offer.

Stop reading and go!

Firstly, it took them a long time to clean a table for us to sit down. Then it took like 20 minutes to order. And then we waited 90 minutes to get any food and each dish came out one at a time like 20 minutes apart, all in random order. Even though asking for soup several times, this came out last. Stopped by last Sunday for dinner after 6p.  Shortly after we got there the restaurant filled up.  One of the best Szechuan restaurants I've been to and will be back.   We tried  multiple dishes, around 9 so we has plenty of leftovers to take home.  Bonus for us since there are not to many Szechuan restaurant in our hood. Great food, great service and great price! Though it take 15 minutes bus from Flushing, but totally worth it!!! Will come back again!!!

The dumplings and cold noodles were particularly tasty at a recent visit. The staff makes up for their lack of English facility with courteousness and effort. Nearly all the food was pleasantly spicy so prepare your palate. And $3 Coronas to wash it down? How can you go wrong... Cash only.

As an unrepentant, slightly masochistic Szechuan fiend, Little Pepper was the deep-Queens mecca that I'd been searching for to satisfy my sick hot-tingly-numb peppercorn fixation. After my first time here, I wanted to come back almost immediately, and so far, most of what I've tried has been excellent. Shamefully, Little Pepper didn't really come on my radar until I read Pete Wells' glowing writeup in the NYT, and when I had access to a car, I decided to make a pilgrimage here.

Little Pepper is a step up from your neighborhood takeout joint, and it's exactly the kind of spot that I would've come to as a child with a giant crowd of my extended family (if they liked Szechuan, that is -- but the decor is classic Chinese family restaurant). The service is polite, if at times slightly brusque, but I was here for the food, and frankly, I'm not going to Szechuan restaurant for white-glove service. Little Pepper, as Wells says, packs the heat!

One thing I would say: you're not going to get the full flavor journey if you don't eat meat here. Lots of dishes rely on meat as a flavoring ingredient even if it's not the star of the plate; if you're looking for a place to go with vegan friends, it would be unfair to take them here. 

Little Pepper's food is vibrant, complex, fragrant, and most importantly, delicious. They manage to nail the spice profile of each dish almost every time, and there's a wide variety of different flavor compositions in the menu. There's plenty of the familiar tingly-hot má là that we know from Szechuan food, along with the cumin-inflected Mongolian influence of the north, in addition to some treacly Chinese American mainstays like orange/General Tso's chicken. I'd recommend sticking to their specialties here, namely, the several-chili-pepper-heat-rating hot stuff.

Things I've ordered and liked:
--Scallion Fried Rice ($5.50): why the heck is it so green? how does it taste like pure, unadulterated scallion juice? what makes it taste even better the next day? I have many questions about this, but like the joker, it's a green thing that is very intriguing and covered in mysteries. It's delicious, just order it.
--Lamb with Scallion ($14.95): "Wow," you might be thinking, "what a boring name!" While that observation is true, YOU ARE WRONG about it being boring, because this has two layers of excitement. One, it comes in a foil packet that you unfold to release a steamy hit of cumin-y lamb-y goodness right into your face tubes, and two, it's just so good. It's a fairly dry fry with a floral, cumin, spicy flavor that is practically addictive.
--Sichuan Style/Chong Qing Chicken ($11.95): this is something I like at pretty much every Szechuan place, and Little Pepper's version has wonderfully textured chicken, an almost choke-inducing number of chilis, and an amazing taste. It's HOT though, so be forewarned. Those peppers ain't a joke.
--Thin Sliced Beef Tendon with Chili Sauce ($7.95): my shameful confession is that normally I despise tendon and find it akin to ripping through rubber bands with my incisors. However, Little Pepper's tendon is REALLY GOOD -- tender, flavorful, interesting, and with just the right amount of chew. The chili sauce doesn't hurt, either.
--Dumplings in Hot Sauce ($4.95): another awful secret of mine? I'm normally kinda "meh" on dumplings, but these were excellent. The skin wasn't too chewy and bland (my usual dumpling complaint) and the sauce/filling were spot-on delicious.
--Shredded pork with noodles: this had an amazing, complex flavor profile and ended up being one of the most popular dishes at our table. Everyone will like it.
--Pickled cucumbers: I order these at every Szechuan restaurant, and you know what? They're hard to screw up, and a necessary antidote to your mouth fire.

Things I've eaten that were good:
--Dan Dan Noodles with Pork ($5.95): I've had a lot of dan dan. Little Pepper's is not the most amazing version of the dish I've had, but worth ordering if you're in the mood for it since it's a reliably executed dish.
--Dried Sauteed String Beans ($7.95): I love the char flavor and never say no to a string bean; if you don't like things that taste vegetal, don't get this

Things I've eaten there were ehhhh:
--Mapo Tofu ($7.95): probably my most controversial opinion in here. Frankly, it needed more savory/umami flavor. Don't get me wrong, there's a lot of umami, but it needed some oomph to add dimension to the silkiness of the tofu, the heat of the chili oil, and the mild beefiness of the meat. It's a very good mapo tofu, but not the best I've ever had.
--Spicy Cold Noodle ($5.95): the cold sesame noodle dish that you'll find in a lot of Szechuan restaurants; Little Pepper's tasted pretty bland. Skip.

PHEW. All this is to say: Little Pepper has my eternal fealty and I'll keep on coming back for that addictive mouth burn. Your tongue will ache, your face will sweat, and the next morning may be rough, but it's totally worth it for the crazy flavor journey!

Little Pepper is so good but such a pain to get to! You should absolutely go if you have access to a car but if not you might have to get a little creative. Unless you live in College Point. What are the rents like there? 

As it is well known, there isn't a ton of English spoken here but it's not that big a deal. No one has gotten my order wrong so whatever.

I've been here twice now and eaten a fair number of dishes, but the menu is massive so I feel like I've barely scratched the surface. 

Among appetizers: The cold beef tendon is excellent, very tender with great spice and a solid tingle. Dan dan noodles are middle of the road-- not the best not the worst. The spicy cold noodle, however, is DYNAMITE. It's surprising because it's just a cloud of cold noodles in a vinaigrette, but the vinaigrette is so intensely flavorful that you won't be able to stop eating. Dumplings in hot sauce are also great-- skins are nice and light, filling is flavorful, and the spicy sauce has (similar to the spicy cold noodle) an enormous flavor.

Veggies are also a standout. On our first night we had pea leaves, which are lightly sauced, but the intense green of the leaves stands on its own, and is a pleasing contrast to more powerfully flavored things you might also have on your table. We also had the dried stir-fried string beans and these are a straight hit-- sauce is great and the beans have great snap.

I, like most humans, read Pete Wells' review of this place. He had a lot of praise for the mapo tofu but I was not as into it. He seemed to feel it was 'nuanced' but I guess I just like big huge flavors in my mapo so I found this a little weak. Not bad just not revelatory.

Meat game is strong at Little Pepper. The cumin lamb and the chongqing chicken are both powerfully flavored and meaty. The portions are huge so if you order them make sure you want spicy lunch the next day.

Like a lot of Chinese restaurants, the beer is nice and cheap. Notably, Heineken is the same price as Tsingtao, which is kinda nice.

Little Pepper is a little bit of a trip, but it's worth making. I definitely recommend going with as large a group of friends as possible-- the menu is enormous and you'll want to try a lot of stuff. Also, friend with a car is pretty key.

I first came to little pepper for the first time a few years ago, it's in a part of Queens that i'd usually rarely be in unless I had a reason to be, one important thing to note is that this place is cash only so keep that in mind. I've been here to dine in and the waiters are very nice, it is spacious inside with plenty of seating, the food great here it's spicy but it's very flavorful, one of the best things here are the dumplings they come in this hot gravy like sauce, majority of the dishes are ordered and served family style, the last find I was here I ordered takeout and got the orange chicken lunch special, it was great and doesn't leave you with that salty thirsty feeling that most general tso type of chicken tends to leave you with, it was flavored perfectly, I highly recommend this place but it loses a star for not accepting credit cards

Authentic Chinese food！My mom and I really like the beef noodles and fried rice～ Compared with the other restaurant in New York，The price is much cheaper but they provides large and delicious portion！Recommend this restaurant if you will stay here for some time～

Disappointed after reading the reviews. Ordered spicy beef noodle soup have to ask where's the beef? Ordered wontons with hot sauce we got wontons and spicy soup. Awful customer service will not be returning again
Returned from a trip to China a month ago. This restaurant provided the atmosphere and cuisine that I dearly miss.

Unbelievable, it's simply just not good food. Now, I'm not a professional food critic or anything, but I know bad food when I taste it. Everything that came out was just drowned in salt. We got the cumin lamb, and it was utterly inedible because of the salt. The flavor is also boring. It's just straight chili flakes on it. There is nothing special about it. The Dan Dan noodles, a specialty of the culture, was a disappointment. Like come on, how can you mess that up? In addition to the saltiness of the noodles, all that we tasted was soy sauce. We also had beef tendons. This was not as bad, but could definitely be much better. On these, I could literally feel the texture of the salt grains in my mouth. How does that even happen? Are there even cooks in the back? My mother had to ask the waitress for a small bowl to pour tea in so that she can mix the food in it so it would tone down the salt in the food. There is absolutely no reason, especially for a restaurant, to have such bad food prepared for customers. Would not come here ever again.

Ordered:
Sliced Beef Tendon
- Not snappy, too mushy
Dan Dan Noodles
- Noodles were too soft
Cumin Lamb
- Average
Green Beans
- Best of the dishes ordered

All dishes were way too salty, almost inedible. 

Food was quick to come out though...

Finally had a chance to visit this hidden gem of authentic home cooking Szechuan food in Queens, absolutely worth the trip. The Home Fish with Minced Pork, of which Pete Wells strongly recommends, is a must try. The fish is tender, which pairs perfectly with the crispy spicy minced pork, the broth is a charming and intriguing pool of chili oil.

Another amazing thing is the pickled Szechuan vegetables, as a Chongqing native, I could tell that this is authentic, the pink little cubes evokes an nostalgic feeling of the first bite of this childhood snack. 

And the little pepper fried rice is the go-to pairing to the pickled veggies.

One thing important for people love trying Szechuan food, is that if it is authentic, then you would have the opportunity to easily distinguish the different types of spicy tastes, it's not vaguely different but somehow good chefs can juxtapose and mingle among different layers and varied mediums quite well, and the chefs of Little Pepper did it.

my second or third time here tonight~ really love this place!
super super delicious! and so authentic!
my favourites are the beef jerky, the arctic surf clam, the spicy cold noodle, the lobster, and actually every dish!
the fish with minced pork is a magic combination with their special sauce, it was once featured on NY Times, and it has multiple layers of flavors -- surprisingly tasty! 
and their fried rice is definitely a must try, soooooo impressive!

This place is magic. I went there last night for the first time. The food was so delicious and authentic. My favorite is the appetizer Spicy Surf Calm (麻辣北极贝). I also strongly recommend the Spicy Sea Bass with Minced Pork. I heard it's the NYTimes restaurant critic Pete Wells' favorite. 

And the price was pretty cheap too! When I posted the photos on Facebook, a friend of mine commented "I came here with a group of 9 people. We ordered constantly for 2 hours, maybe 20 dishes total. The bill came, and we all held our breath... It cost $20 per person."

Another special thing about this restaurant is the art work on the wall. Love those paintings! So talented. They are actually all by the owners' son, who is an artist and a chef now working in the restaurant.

I will definitely recommend this place to all my Chinese and American friends!

Love this place when it was in downtown flushing !!! It's kinda far from where I live but wouldnt mind going there at all! The whole fish and beef jerk is sooooooo amazing! And so happy to see they have summer dessert now. Really love the jelly ~~~~

Some of the best Sichuan food I've had since living in China. Was a bit skeptical given the odd location but the place was clean and dishes were legit. The shuizhu yu (boiled spicy fish) was A++ and a bit cheaper than I've seen in other local Chinese restaurants. Can't wait to go back again and try some of the lunch specials!
Just had the dan dan noodles that everyone's been talking about & o-m-g. I think this is going to be my new favorite dish. So spicy and tasty. It was minced pork over noodle. It was unbelievable.

My family & I love this place!! We had a wonderful big family birthday party in May (my 60th and I am sorry it took me this long to write a review),  They couldn't have been nicer or more generous. Our meal was delicious, well-timed - honestly perfect. We took 50 guests from NYC & the Hudson Valley. Easy to park. We had an array of meat, fish, noodle and vegetarian dishes, and everything was great. We have also been MANY times for regular meals. I highly recommend Little Pepper. Enjoy!

I'll keep it short: The food tastes like your tongue is being hugged by spicy angels. The décor is plain and clean with some surprising type of art for this type of restaurant. The service is quick and comes with what amounts to bare minimum of a smile on the waiter's face.

The food though, WOW. Flavorful, spicy, creative, just plain delicious. The scallion green rice are incredible as the hot potato fries. The Dan Dan noodles are Damn damn delicious. 

Not for people on diets or aversion to spicy foods.

The food was really good, my girlfriend and I thought that it would probably be a bust because it was so empty. But we where please antsy surprised. The food was tasty, the presentation was not over the top primarily basic but tasty. I had hoped for a full bar but settled for there 5 choice of beers and other non alcoholic beverages. I can't wait to go back

Mapo tofu-very good. Tender and flavourful tofu. Medium spicy. Sautéed luffa-good. Fresh and juicy. Dandan noodle-average. Not as authentic. Chewy noodles. A little spicy. Rabbit Szechuan style-average. A lot of ingredients. Flavourful lotus roots, potato fries, celery, onions, shallots. Heavily-spiced-to-cover-the-unfreshness rabbit meat. White rice-average. Well cooked. A little hard.

DOES NOT DO DELIVERY.
DOES NOT ACCEPT CREDIT CARDS.
CASH ONLY.
THEY DO NOT SPEAK ENGLISH, AT ALL.
$45 for 4 entrees, better be freaking good, with sizeable portions. So far I am thoroughly unimpressed and feel deceived by the yelp reviews. Will update and edit once I have tried the food, but I want it to be on record that their "service" is EXTREMELY POOR.

One word. Overrated. Two words. Not authentic. Szechuan cuisine is world renowned for not only it's spiciness but the numbness of its peppercorn. This place totally caters to Americans.

The dishes lacked not only numbness but spiciness. I don't think they are using the correct variety of chili peppers or peppercorn. We ordered the beef trip appetizer (lacking beef brisket and spiciness), Dan Dan noodle (wrong type of noodles and flavor), chongqing chicken (dry), lamb with cumin (mediocre), and the fish in soup base (fish had zero flavor). 

If I don't know what Szechuan food is supposed to taste like, these dishes would have all been pretty okay except for the fish, which was absolutely horrendous. The fish had no taste. At all! They also just used the root of the napa vegetable...what happened to the leaves?

Needless to say, I'm never going back. Szechuan Gourmet will be the only Szechuan place I'll visit in flushing.

Great food, fast service, good price. I first found the place when I discovered they were one of the few places in NYC with DanDan Noodles. Since then they have been a lunch time favorite the double cooked pork is fantastic as is the shredded beef with spicy pepper. 

Remember its cash only. They are old school like that.

Cannot say enough about this place, the food was amazing. The cabbage with hot peppers was actually fairly mild and cooked perfectly, tender but retaining a mild bite, the scallion rice was equally enjoyable in its flavorful simplicity. The lamb in hot and spicy sauce was rated a two pepper dish and while it had some heat it was very manageable and delicious. Lastly we had the beef with scallions, a basic but well made standard dish.  Service was friendly and very polite, a few food restrictions were accommodated with no issues. As some have stated the staffs English is somewhat basic but  before actually placing our order they had us review the actual order sheet to insure they got the order right, a nice touch to prevent any miscommunication. Portions were generous and had a nice clean taste, no starchy heavy sauces to bog down the taste of the main ingredients.  The place itself is nicely lit and comfortable to be in and the bathroom was super clean, a good reflection on how a place is managed. This is a genuine Chinese restaurant so there are many non Americanized selections for those with an adventurous bent. College Point is definitely out of the way and driving here is the best way to go as public transportation will be a bit of a pain, but the food is so good here you will find the trip well worth it.

If i am not dining in, then i am ordering take out from here at least every other week. The service is pretty much what i have come to expect from most chinese restaurants- there's always someone peeling green beans, always a bit of yelling, they pretty much leave you alone, and it always takes forever to refill your tea. 

But the food is their crown jewel. They have many dishes that you can find in other restaurants, but they just know how to do it right. Their cold sesame noodle is sauced nicely. Their dried sauteed green beans are soooo flavorful. They have an amazing chicken and peanuts hot pepper dish. And the beef tendon app is the BEST.

If you ever find yourself in college point, this is NOT a place to pass up!
need to wait for dinner. the cuisines are just so-so. but at least is not bad in college point
Decent food, but a bit pricy for what you get... There are better options a few minutes away in flushing. Their sauce with the Scallion Pancake is pretty good.

Very pleasantly surprised with Little Pepper. The ingredients are high quality and very fresh. The entrees are very well built and attractive. The flavors all come together very nicely and in good balance. The hot & sour soup is amazing. Scallion pancakes are the best I've had in searching all over. The spicy peanut chicken is perfect. Definitely a new destination - no matter where I'm coming from.
I GIVE A 5 STAR because most of the 8 dish i order was good. this food is spicy if you just dont eat the pepers than it's not so hot

This is a great Szechuan style restaurant in College Point. They have inexpensive lunch specials. For under $10 you can get a hot and sour soup, and a dish with rice.  I like the Kung Pao Chicken (spicy chicken with peanuts) because it exemplifies their cooking style.  The place isn't fancy but it's casual, clean and one of the better spots in the area for Asian cooking.

Mapo Tofu: Lacked flavor, nothing special

So ok, nothing special. If I was to eat this type of food I'd go to New World Mall in Flushing.

Had high expectations. Wasn't spicy/hot, wasn't tasty, completely empty restaurant and the waiter was so disinterested he went to the kitchen and didnt  come back out till we were ready to leave. We could have walked out without paying, no one cared.  2 thumbs down, do not waste your time.

I checked the reviews before coming here and Noticed they were mixed so I decided to give it a shot myself.  The food was just okay to be honest. My go to place is usually mama lee but she was closed so I decided to come here.  They try to copy her food but don't come close. The flavors just aren't there unfortunately. I wouldn't come back here.
This is hands down the best Chinese food I've had outside of China. The cold spicy noodles are amazing! The staff is friendly and the prices are reasonable. I only wish I lived closer!

I have had this place bookmarked for a while but the idea of having authentic Chinese food in the middle of College Point, Queens made me super skeptical. God dammit was I wrong. The food was excellent! When they say a dish was spicy, it was spicy and when they said a dish wasn't spicy, well it wasn't lol The decor is very simple Chinese restaurant decor but I thought the service was friendly and helpful. The one drawback, the restaurant is kinda inconvenient without a car, it's accessible by bus but it is a little bit of a pain. Overall, a must visit for awesome Chinese food. And the dish are large so sharing would be ideal.
