Preserved Egg w. Green Pepper- This was a shock for me since I am not normally a fan of the preserved egg in congee since it is too aggressive of a flavor for me but the one here was excellent and my favorite dish of the night. The texture of the egg was great, the yolk wasn't too strong and the chili oil was great. Highly recommend. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=ZyHa9jn0el8FmhNZHt2nPw&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Sliced Pork Belly w. Chili-Garlic Sauce- The pork belly was a generous order and it was perfectly tender. It was kinda like a braised pork belly, it was a bit salty and a bit sweet but really good. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=7GywLTZYOhdXHp5O6a7-Yw&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Spicy Cold Noodle- I was surprised how good this dish came out. The noodles looked like your basic Lo Mein noodles but this dish was served cold. The texture of the noodles were wonderful and the chili oil had really good flavor. The sweetness did surprise me a bit but the dish as a whole was well balance and the dish was not really spicy. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=QWn-9Cr0NcicZ-A9sj89AA&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Griddle Cooked Mushroom w. Preserved Pork- This dish felt like somewhat of a healthy dish but I enjoyed the flavors. The preserved pork was pork belly that had an interesting flavor from being preserved, it was like pork with a little bit of a funk but a good kind of funk. The mushrooms were a big part of the dish but it was like a very dry mushroom, not sure the name of it. It's really dry and kinda fibrous but I enjoyed the flavor and the leftovers heated up well. This is not the most exciting dish but I enjoyed it. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=7UBRu8eIvRpZBTjEAqqEWA&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Scallion Fried Rice- The first thing that has to be mentioned is the color, it is so damn green! Anywho, the scallion fried rice was good, I enjoyed the flavor and the texture was nice but it really didn't stand out as much as I thought it would, well besides the color. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=KPzHfZXgrC8ySs5qHHglWA&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Mapo Tofu- The flavor on this wasn't bad, the sauce was good but I remember the tofu being really plain. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=Tdu7B0oxHJwQT3yb9nHmXg&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Lamb w. Hot & Spicy Sauce (w. Cumin)- This dish was kind of a let down for me, it was super interesting because your tongue will get really numb from the spices but I felt the the dish was over seasoned. The flavor was good and it was tender but it was too salty/overaggressive in flavor. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=l07yq0u5Hj_Ht6O_GjlEow&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Thin Sliced Beef Tendon w/ Chili Sauce- The tendon was good but I wished it was a little more tender, I felt like it was more chewy than what I had at other places. Also, the dish has some heat and it will number your mouth like the lamb. Overall, I thought this was skippable. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=pbO1N3hKg7ycI_mu3awccQ&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

The Little Pepper was definitely not the spot for me. My family liked it and thought it was good but it wasn't the type of spicy I was looking for. Szechuan style dishes can be numbing in the tongue so if you're not into that then this might not be the spot for you. Some dishes we ordered were the chili braised fish filet, beef and tripe, preserved egg with green pepper, dan dan noodles, and a spicy chicken dish. Overall, all the dishes were great but the type of spicy was just not for me.

I did try to come here on a Thursday afternoon to find out that they are not open on Thursdays. Compared to eating in Flushing, this place is a lot more spacious and relaxing. The food was great. One of the dishes I tried, the scallion fried rice, at first, I didn't quite like it for the first few bites but as I had more, I really liked it. I will be coming here more often.

We really enjoy our meals at little pepper. Authentic Chinese without all the oil you usually get with this type of food. Our favorites are the dumplings sesame chicken double cooked pork and the lamb with cumin. Give it a shot if you are looking for a authentic Chinese meal.

I went to this place because my Mother-in-Law lives in College Point and I read an excellent review in the New York Times. This is truly an excellent option in College Point, really an oasis in a neighborhood with very few tasty food options.

We took our whole family out and everyone really loved it. The price is super affordable and there are options that are fresh, which is helpful if you don't want to eat a greasy meal. 

I tell people whenever I can about this place and would highly recommend that others give it a chance. It's worth traveling for.

Also, pro-tip: come here for a big family dinner and pick up the check! You'll look like a big shot without making a big dent in your wallet :P

Food: 1.5/5.0
Service: 2.5/5.0
Value: 3.0/5.0
Decor: 3.0/5.0
Overall: 1.5/5.0 

Wow.  So disappointed.  The dishes I had alternated between too much numbing pepper/not enough hot to fine on hot/not enough numbing.  The hot and sour soup had no sour.  The dan dan noodles were just bad.  I have no idea what Yelp is thinking on this one - or did the kitchen really just have a truly truly bad day?  Maybe the ratings are just inflated by the lack of competition in the area.  I have no interest in returning.
Great 四川 restaurant,  made me feel like I was back in 中国。nice dandan noodles,  dumplings and dried beef.  Thumbs-up!

It's hard to get me to ever rate Sichuan food badly. If it's authentically salty and spicy, I'm all about it. Little Pepper's gotta be REAL up your alley if you're willing to come out to far-out, MTA inaccessible College Point but hubs and I have a car so it was not too bad. Came just before 9 on a Saturday and there were plenty of people dining but also plenty of seating. Ambiance is a bit sterile but service is prompt, fast, friendly, and the space is moderately big. The food had a slightly different Sichuan spin on it, things being cooked a bit differently, and things being  - in my opinion - less spicy than usual.  

We ordered the: 

- Cold Sesame Noodles, pretty good. Had a sour, tangy taste to be an alternative to dan dan
- Dumplings in chili oil - always delicious, plentiful, and filing
- The chongqing chicken - delicious flash fried nuggets of spicy chicken with LOTS of dried chilies, aka "dry pepper chicken" but this wasn't breaded at all which I honestly appreciated 
-The kung pao chicken - honestly this was bad. It was like a teriyaki chicken with mirin - not spicy, no peanuts really..  worth skipping
-The spicy cumin beef - very tasty. So heavily seasoned with cumin so be prepared, with sauteed onion and pepper. Not very spicy. 
-The scallion fried rice. This was actually quite good and super flavorful. Eggy, but scallion-y as well - don't miss it. 

All in all, it was pretty good. I'd come back but not go out of my way.  Prices are typical, $12-15 per dish. The appetizers were cheaper with dan dan and scallion fried rice being $7 or so.
If you love spicy foods then Little Pepper had what you need! Their mapo tofu & Dan Dan noodles were delicious.  The dumpling in hot chili oil was pretty good but not the best I've had.

Claim them-self was a Michellin was a joke, so overrated food was awful, cold dish came out frozen with icy taste, hot dish ingredients was smell and rotten but use a lot of chilly oil cover so can fool around, inside restaurant is hot no a/c on even 85degree, will not recommend or u go try with your own risk! 
P.s. Follow up this post at next morning, we all went bath room crazy! Zero star if i can!

I got takeout here over the weekend and it was quick and efficient. The staff didn't speak English perfectly, but you can easily understand with their descriptive menu.

We ordered:
1.) Scallion fried rice ($6.95): Oily, but yummy! Simply just scallion puree, eggs and rice
2.) Beef with scallion ($15.95): Very tender beef and lots of onions and scallions
3.) Fried chicken nugget with garlic sauce ($11.95): Very similar to General Tso's Chicken

Everything was super oily, but of course delicious. The prices are on the expensive-r side, especially for College Point, but Little Pepper is certainly not any ordinary Chinese Restaurant. Although we didn't really order anything Sichuan-y, they definitely incorporate a spicy kick and fresher protein to these typical Chinese dishes.

We trekked all the way past Flushing to Whitestone, an area I'm not too familiar with. The restaurant is deep in Whitestone and I mean DEEP! The restaurant is clean modern and well lit. Hubster and I ordered the spicy tendon, the spicy chicken (cold dish), sugar vinegar cabbage (direct Chinese translation), spicy fish filet casserole (water boiled fish) and the cumin lamb baked in foil. The spicy tendon cut a little thicker than normal was nice. I liked that it was cut a tad thicker giving it better texture. Spice level was medium, so tolerable for everyone. The spicy chicken was good. It had a sweet spiciness which was really nice. I would say its a little sweeter than the other sichuan places on my rotation. But still my mouth was on fire after two pieces. The spicy fish casserole was amazing! Lotta fish. Good amount of wood ear. And good spice level. Tasty! The cumin spiced lamb in foil was great as well. Super flavorful and nice kick! The sugar vinegar cabbage was the perfect dish to calm the heat down. Anytime my mouth was buzzing and numb from the peppercorns of the other dishes, I had some of the cabbage. The sweet and sour was of the cabbage was delicious! I could eat so much of this with rice!! When it came time for the bill, I was pleasantly surprised to see them come with the little machine that you get when you pay for a restaurant bill in Europe and Canada and parts of Asia. With so much credit card fraud going on everywhere this is a welcome thing to see. And just for this I think they deserve an extra star for being technology savvy!!! Def making the trek back here for another mind numbing experience!

Parking: Street

Inside: Only a few tables. Fortunately, my dad and I were the only ones when we arrived (30minutes into opening). And I think 1 guy came in during our time there. Others were mostly pick-up. One guy had a HUGE pick-up order so I'm assuming ordering for parties is a go as well. 

Staff: Friendly. No complaints. 

Food: So we came here because my dad wanted to try their Dan Dan noodles (he's been on a hunt for one he likes and he came across this one via Yelp). So he ordered them, obviously. He said it wasn't the style/taste he was searching for but still good ($5.95). 
In addition, we got the wonton in hot sauce ($5.95) which was pretty darn good. In the pic, it looks like it's drenched in hot oil but it eating it wasn't as bad and not that heavy. Order plain white rice to go with it. It'll be perfect! (We didn't because we got fried rice).
Also got the chicken in chongqing style (3 pepper marks; $12.95). It was hot but a good-flavorful, burns your tongue hot. So overall it was good but the pepper to chicken ratio was a little whomp whomp. Wish there was a little more chicken and bigger chunks of it. 
Got the fried with Sichuan brined vegetable ($5.95) as well. I really liked it. Nice & spicy and yummy. I give it a two thumbs up. 
Don't get the egg drop soup ($1.95). It was flavorless, unfortunately. 

Overall, food and experience was good! Since we went for the spicy route at this visit, we'll prob try some non-spicy or more mild spicy dishes at our next visit. But my dad is still in the hunt for more Dan Dan noodle places.lol.

I don't Normally give reviews on yelp. But this chinese restaurant in college point really got my nerves.  I have never had Kong Pao chicken as bad as this (picture below)in "authentic" Chinese restaurant that specializes in Sichuan foods. Only over cooked chicken and peanuts in dark sweet sauce no other ingredients like they should have.  Flushing food Ct can make much better than this and it is definitely not worth 13 dollars!!

If you're looking to eat some authentic Szechuan food, this place is amazing. I haven't had everything yet on the menu, but every item I've had has been great. Personally, I love going with larger groups and ordering a bunch of dishes, family-style. If there are leftovers because of over-ordering, the dishes are great to keep overnight in the fridge for a satisfying work lunch!

If I could give them 0 star, I would.  I was there years ago,  and the food was good at the time,  so I wanted to take my family there tonight but we were all very VERY disappointed!  We ordered "fish in spicy soup base","Griddle cooked mushroom with preserved pork","crab with chili pepper" and "Dumpling in hot sauce".  The only dish that was good was the "dumpling in hot sauce",  the other dishes was just way overly salty!  We all just took one bite and we couldn't eat the rest. You can literally feel the salt in your mouth.  Yeah! It was that bad!!  I really don't how they get all the good reviews!

After we complained, they didn't say anything and just took the dishes back to the kitchen, we have no idea what they were doing with it, but it came back 2 minutes later and taste no different.  When we complained again, they gave us an attitude saying this is how it should taste. Now I've been to many Szechuan restaurants before and never were the foods this salty. We had such a bad experience tonight and I really hope they taste their own food before serving. 

We always pass by Little Pepper on the way home and always looking forward to dining in but we will never return after this.

I had this place bookmarked for forever and finally got to try! I called ahead and had it as pickup so I can't say much for the service in the restaurant. 

We had the Dan Dan Noodles and the scallion fried rice. The servings are really big, I can say each entree can fill up 2 people easily.
I've never tried Dan Dan noodles but the one from here was very delicious. It was spicy and numbing and my tongue was very numb after and I couldn't finish it. The scallion fried rice was very very green.. I don't know how they make it so green but it was delicious!

Prices are fair and the food was good. Parking is pretty easy.
Best Sichuan food in the town. Highly recommended steamed chicken w. Special chili sauce, dumpling in hot sauce, dried sautéed string bean!!!

This place is bomb! My friend took us here and this is the best Szechuan food I had in NY. 

There are only a few tables and this is a popular neighborhood spot in college point. 

Every dish I had was super tasty, but I wouldn't recommend the intestines. I prefer it to be deep fried but instead, it was stir-fried which was indeed very pungent. 

I also can't wait to come back to try the scallion fried rice!

Omg this is the best cumin lamb that I have ever eating before. So fresh....amazing balanced flavors with the onions, cilantro and spice!!! I asked to make it a little less spicy than normal just because I was afraid that would be too spicy and I'm glad that I did. Totally recommend this dish and place.
Too expensive compare with the quality of the food. Ordered a preserved pork, gave me a regular pork. Won't go again.

if I could then I would give negative star, we ordered over the phone for delivery, they said 25 minutes would be the delivery time. We waited 1 hour 35 minutes and nothing happened. We called several times but nobody speak English.

Somewhat likely to recommend friends to this place. Went there with a couple of friends for the dinner on weekends. Their dishes were ok, but not authentic Szechuan dishes. Employees were very nice and cook waiting time just about right before you start complaining.

I finally tried some food from here that only took 2 years lol a friend recommended 2 dishes to try. Spicy meatballs and the other was dried string beans in some kind of garlic stuff. I thought the meatballs were awesome would definitely recommend those to anyone, the string bean thingy wasn't a big fan of, it had a weird texture  but my brother loved them

Meh. Ate hear a couple of times. Not that impressed either time. This is a place where "cool" people go to experience Chinese food. You can get better food in downtown Flushing, however you probably won't look as cool.

Wow so good I'm writing this review as we wait for our check. 

If you're a real fan of Sichuan then this place is definitely for you. They don't skimp out on the spice and the peppercorns so you get the exact Sichuan numbing experience you're looking for!! We got the staple of boiled/braised fish along with the minced pork with clear noodles, dan dan noodles, and scallion fried rice. My favorites were the clear noodles and boiled fish. I'm not a fan of onions but my bf loved the scallion fried rice! You could skip the dan dan noodles. 

The portions were very generous. We have leftovers enough for another full meal. Everything came out to only $43. Also the staff is super attentive and courteous. Love this place!! Definitely want to come back and try the mapo tofu and more (:
So darn good. Everything. Every dish. Every flavor. I want to say here that we have never seen a cleaner restaurant. Dining room, bathroom and kitchen were spotless.

Love this place!!! 

I have never enjoyed shezchuan food until coming here. Everything is great and reasonably priced. I love the lamb, scallion fried rice and Dan Dan noodle. 

If you're ever in college point and want to switch up your chinese food craving, check this spot out! You will not be disappointed.

What a find! Excellent food in a nondescript storefront restaurant. Ordered Scallion Fried Rice, Dan Dan noodles, fried pork and fish. Everything was excellent, and large enough portions to take home. Spicy and yummy. The desserts were not so great, but hardly a chink when the main course was so yummy!

I would love to give this place 5 stars. However, as a regular customer here, the owner (who clearly knows me since I basically come once a week) once denied me a table for reservations and didn't bother apologizing or explaining what happened. Whenever I go, the place is typically empty so it was a huge surprise for it to be packed with menus on the table hinting at reservations. Okay fine, I got unlucky that day. I don't come here for their service lets be clear, but their food is honestly pretty good. My favorite is their cabbage, hot dumplings, and their fish. My friend likes their cumin lamb and chicken (I have no idea what the full name is because I usually order it in Chinese, but it's spicy). Service isn't an issue from the waitresses so if you like Sichuan, check it out!

I ordered the Dan Dan noodles and asked it to be "regular" spicy. This is my first time eating Sichuan food so I erred on the side of caution. Unfortunately, I was too cautious. I sadly didn't have to forcibly chug water down my throat to curb the infamous burning sensation because... there was none.

Next, I had the pleasure of trying the double cooked pork. This piece of beauty was chock full of pork fat, which I normally love but this was just overkill. I was just shoving spoonfuls of warm pork oil into my numb happy mouth. Thankfully, Little Pepper made this dish a smudge healthier by throwing in some cabbage, scallions and onions. Despite the significantly increased chances of a heart attack, the double cooked pork was delicious. Similar to Dan Dan noodles, it was delightfully salty and slightly spicy. The double cooked pork came with a bowl of white rice which was the ideal carb for the exuberant flavors. The only downside, other than the clogged arteries from the pork fat, is it's too oily. So really, this dish should be called double clogged arteries.
Amazing dumplings  in hot chili  oil!!  great prices awesome service.  Came here by accident lol for lunch  so glad I did! Will be ordering for take

I went here for the first time last night and I thought it was excellent! I had been wanting to go here since the NY Times review in 2016 and finally made it. 

They were very accommodating with making everything vegetarian for me and all the food we ordered was delicious. I especially liked the dried string beans with pepper and the vegetarian dan dan noodles. The cold mushroom appetizer was also interesting and a nice contrast to everything else we ordered. I also ordered the cabbage with red pepper and the same string bean dish for my parents who lived in Hong Kong for 7 years and they both thought it was delicious and authentic.

Also, I accidentally left my scarf at the table and they saved it for me to pick up which was honest. I will definitely be back!

Wow! Everything was amazingly tasty and super affordable. Can't beat these prices and the service. 
Ordered:
String beans- delicious but spicy. So good that I just kept eating them even though it was spicy. 
Scallion fried rice- so bomb. This & string beans are a must. Compliments each other perfectly. Love the rice texture. Not a strong scallion taste for those who don't like scallions.
Dumplings in spicy sauce- this is the best sauce ever! Not spicy, it's sweet but delicious.
Mapo tofu- it had good flavors but not enough meat. Nonetheless it was delicious.
All this was under $37.
Can't wait to come back and try other sechuan spicy goodness.
Best spicy Chinese food in area . Clean friendly fast and fresh , try eggplant in garlic sauce and try mapo tofu amazing all good here..

I love this place. This restaurant is my fiancé and I go-to spot !! We eat here so often this waitress already know what table we normally sit at and our order. We typically order their Szechuan chicken chicken, pea shoots vegetable and every now and then cold noodles and/or wonton dumplings.

This is a hidden gem in a quiet Queens neighborhood. The staff is super friendly and attentive and the food always tastes fresh (and spicy)  The Chong Qing Chicken is a must! With a glass of beer on the side. You won't be disappointed.

Best Chinese food, from any region, that I've ever had the pleasure of eating. $60 for round trip ubers to and from here being the only downside, but honestly being so out of the way keeps this place a hidden gem. 

Cumin lamb, salt and pepper shrimp, charred stringbeans, ma po tofu, cold pork belly with ginger, mashed cucumber with ginger, braised sliced fish in soup, sichuan style chicken, dumplings, dan dan noodles, scallion fried rice are usually what I order. Usually just between myself and another person, since I go there so rarely and desperately crave leftovers the day after. 

Just go and order the stuff they're known for - it's an experience and probably one of the 10 best restaurants I've ever had the pleasure of knowing. Nothing else is like it here in NYC.
My favourite Sichuan food restaurant.They do the real original Sichuan taste .no add other .

To be honest, I'm a little shocked by all the other reviews... After reading them, I was expecting one of the most amazing culinary experiences of my life, and I did not get that.

The service was good, because the restaurant was deserted. Anytime my family whispered anything, they came to address our needs thinking we were requesting something. The food came unnaturally fast. It was borderline sketchy. The first dish came within 4 minutes, and the rest came within 10 minutes after ordering.

Honestly, the portions are small. Everything was laced in peppercorns and salt. The string beans didn't taste like anything except spiciness. My family was not a huge fan of the cumin lamb. The only good dish was the scallion fried rice but even that was a little bit too salty. Maybe I ordered all the wrong things but I seem to be what everyone else ordered on yelp. To be honest, you can probably find better food in Flushing. I don't know if it's worth traveling all the way to College Point to try this restaurant.
Good food but horrible service, big language barrier and after sending the string beans back for being to spicy they tried charging me for the dish still.  Not acceptable

What a hidden little gem! I couldn't have been more impressed with my visit. I came for dinner with my mom on a Friday night around 730pm & by 8pm we were done, stuffed out of minds. That's how fast & great the service is. Super cute & CLEAN restaurant. They were even playing music in the background. 

We ordered the scallion fried rice (my fav), chicken with string beans, beef with scallions & pork dumplings. Everything was so savory & delicious that even after we left we could still taste the flavors. Keep in mind most of their dishes are spicy. The chicken dish wasn't as bad but it has a nice kick. The dumplings have a sweet taste to them but come in a spicy sauce & are topped with sesame seeds & scallions. The portions are huge - even though we shared we were so full & still had extra to take home. Super affordable & they now accept cards & PayPal as well. Definite must try if you're in CP. Can't wait to come back & try other dishes!

Little Pepper is truly something special. It is tucked away on College Point Boulevard and genuinely one of the best Chinese restaurants I have tried. The interior is clean and nicely decorated, original artwork is displayed on the walls. Prices are reasonable and portions are generous. I am a fan of the scallion fried rice, General Tso's Chicken, Tofu in Brown Sauce, and their dumplings. Also, hot tea is provided at the beginning of the meal for free, which is an appreciated gesture. I recommend this restaurant always to anyone in the mood for tasty and wholesome Chinese food.
This place is legit. The string beans and mapo tofu are not to be missed. The dan dan noodles are very good too. If you ever find yourself passing through the neighborhood it's worth a stop.

This place is one of my favorite restaurants. The place is so clean and the food so delicious I keep going back to eat my way through the menu! Favorites: beef with scallion, dumplings in chili oil, wonton soup, sautéed green beans (the best in NYC), cumin lamb, twice cooked pork, pea shoots with garlic! I eat so much I have to move to a bigger table!!' Go to this place and fall in love!

First timer but definitely not my last
i cant believe i haven't tried this place out sooner, i live a few minutes away and was super surprised at how good everything was
the service was fast i came in on a Sunday around 830
i had the string beans, scallion fried rice, dan dan noodles and the dumplings in hot sauce.
the sauce the dumplings come in go great with the scallion friend rice !

This is probably the best Chinese restaurant I've been to in the New York area  Everything we got (dan dan noodles, scallion rice, changqing chicken, cumin lamb and fish fillet in red chili oil) was fantastic, with amazingly well-balanced flavors. For those who are sensitive to spice, it's Sichuan so it's spicy, but the spice isn't overwhelming to the point of numbing you. The waiter was also very nice and helpful. Will definitely be back.

Not gonna lie I came here because I was craving for dan dan noodle and it was sort of close to walking distance from college point movie theater.

Chicken in garlic sauce 2/5 - ok, so idk where to start. uhm, so this does not taste anything near garlic at all. It tasted exactly like general tso chicken you could get at a American Chinese takeout place. the meat was a little fatty for me as well, I thought it would be more like a minced chicken in garlic sauce so I did not expected it to be like a big chunk of chicken. BUT, if you like general tso chicken then it is not a bad choice for you. otherwise, do not get it! 

Dan dan noodle 2.5/5 - not gonna lie, I expected a lot esp after one of my friend rave and the reviews that I read. I was expecting like a tingly and numbing feeling but I ate this feeling like I was eating spicy oil with no slight hint of spiciness. 

Scallion fried rice 2/5 - so disappointed! this dish was too oily for my taste! It was literally all green coloring oil from the plate and the spoon that I used to scoop it to my plate. Couldn't taste any scallion flavor at all  - felt like I was eating plain white rice except it is green. 

Dried sautéed string bean 3.5/5 - this wasn't bad but the pickled veggie (?) that came with it helped the dish a lot. Was not spicy at all. 

Hot & sour soup 4/5 - this was sooo gooood! not gonna lie, this is one of the dish that i was lending toward to the whole meal. Not gonna explain how this taste because it tasted exactly how it taste.

Sliced pork belly w chili garlic sauce 4/5 - this is my fav out of all the dishes that I ordered. This is also one of the dish that i was lending toward to the whole meal. This, I def can feel the Szechuan spicy. Full of flavor and the scallion helped a lot. HIGHLY REC. 

Not too sure if I would travel all the way here again, but it was nice to try for once!

You would never think to get quality Asian food in an area like college point. But the little pepper has amazing food Chinese food that tops any Chinese restaurant in queens I've visited so far. I don't have to travel into Chinatown anymore for super authentic Chinese food. 

I came around 5pm and I was attended quickly. Service was great but parking can be somewhat troublesome. 

Back to the food. The mean the menu is jammed packed with great food option. I ordered the sesame chicken and the flavor was simply great. He plates are what I would say big enough for two so come with an appetite if your coming alone. Enjoy I hope this helps some.

First time venturing out to this part of Queens and had no idea there'd be this hidden gem. Really flavorful, delicious, and massive portions. We ordered the griddled mushrooms, scallion fried rice, mapo tofu, chongqing chicken, and beef ox tripe for three people which was ambitious but everything on the menu sounded good. Restaurant itself is clean and service was fine.
Love this place! My new fave, food is really good and quick service. The Dumplings are amazing, definitely a good place to try out.

This is one of the more well known restaurants in College Point and it is for good reason. The food is really flavorful and the service is fantastic. This is the perfect place for people who like spicy foods. However, if you're like me and you can't really eat anything spicier than curry, then this may not be the place for you. They do have non spicy options but they specialize in Sichuan cuisine so it is best to try what they specialize in. It isn't overly expensive and it's never too crowded.

Their food is GREAT!! Ambience and service too! My husband and I immediately recommended this place to our families and friends, they're heading here for dinner tonight. Haha! You'll not regret this place, come for the spicy lamb cumin, mapo taufu, and long beans!! We'll be trying other dishes next time :)

So many amazing restaurants have been opening in Manhattan, that I just haven't had a chance to make it to College Point for the new (to me) location of Little Pepper; I went to the old location a few times (loved the shredded radish & the braised eel!) and have heard enough good things about it recently to pique my interest, and decided to go today: a rainy day, election day, when I had a bit of time to spare. And I wish I hadn't. Everything was so bland, I'm not sure if they gave me the watered-down tourist version (does such a thing even exist in this area?), but honestly the only discernible flavors were salt & sugar, but thankfully some sichuan peppercorns...

very clean and friendly staff. I hate to give a 3 star review since the staff is so nice but i didn't love the food. I tried their popular dishes like scallion fried rice, spicy chicken, cumin beef, cumin lamb, and string beans.  I am a HUGE fan of Spicy and Tasty in Flushing (sadly they closed their doors) and was hoping Little Pepper would be the place to meet my szechuan cravings.  But it wasn't to be. The cumin beef and lamb were not at all spicy and had way too much cumin powder.  I missed the szeuchan peppercorn's mouth numbing spiciness. Scallion fried rice was very greasy and didn't have much flavor.  It also had a strange smell that wasn't pleasant. Spicy chicken was pretty good though. it had a nice kick but was coated thickly in sesame seeds.

This restaurant feels kind of random in this area, but is much welcomed. Seeing foodbaby frequent this place often and being a queens native, I've been dying to try. Perk, not having to venture into flushing for Szechuan food! 

Everything we ordered was above my expectations. The mapo tofu was the right amount of spice and numbing. The string beans were flavorful and fresh. The string beans were flavorful and fresh. The hot pepper chicken was one of my faves. Super crunchy and slightly spicy. Also got the fried rice that was really fragrant and infused with scallion oil, but it kind of got lost eating it with all the other spicy dishes. We got the fish stew which was good, but a bit bland compared to everything else. I was really impressed with the taste and quality of the food and the prices were decent too.

Everything we ordered was good. Standouts were the dumplings, broccoli with dry pepper, and the shrimp fried rice. Restaurant is very clean and has beautiful artwork on display. Service was polite and attentive. I'll come back for more.

It's becoming a trend that authentic Asian spots are popping up on the outskirts of Flushing, which makes sense being that the competition is getting more and more vigorous. This place is a diamond in the rough being in College Pt where the choices aren't exactly in abundance. Maybe it's a sign of the next hip location? Whatever the case may be, Little Pepper is worthy enough to venture to avoiding the overly congested food mecca that Flushing has become, especially for Szechuan cuisine. 

Being on the outskirts of Flushing, the food here is excellent and can compete with the best of them. The flavors are a bit toned down especially the spice level which I didn't mind because some of the more authentic spots in Flushing attempt to kill you with spices sometimes. Everything was seasoned well and portions were on par with prices, it's easily going to be a choice for me to avoid going into Flushing for my Szechuan fix. Overall satisfying and will definitely be back is a big statement for such a little pepper, but it's true nonetheless. 

Stay fat mother suckers
Horrible undercooked chicken and everything was so bland like hospital food. Never again.

An easy 4.5! An intense hankering for Sichuan food but not wanting to fight through the traffic and people of Flushing, we stumbled on this place. When we arrived on a Friday night, there was only one other couple but that didn't deter M and I. We were quickly seated and given menus and tea.

Since this is our first time here, we tend to stick to dishes we already know to see how different places compare. All of the food came out in a hurry, piping hot and with large portions! The spice level wasn't as high as other restaurants but it was nothing to complain about. Our favorite was probably the fish in spicy hot oil. The scallion fried rich was nice but a tad too oily. We took a portion home and I think it can be mixed with some plain jasmine rice and it will just as tasty! 

I actually appreciated that the wait staff left us to our dinner but were quick to come assist us if we

What a spicy surprise, little pepper would not disappoint when your spicy craving hits. We ordered beef ox tripe chili $11.95, thin sliced beef tendon $11.95, preserved egg green pepper $7.95, chicken chonqing sty $13.95, braised sliced fish spicy soup $15.95, griddle cook mushroom preserve pork $19.95, and scallion fried rice $6.95. Top favorites are the ox tripe, beef tendon, chicken, and fried rice because they are just so well seasoned with the flavor and crunchiness They do tend to be on the saltier side so it goes well with rice. Cozy restaurant with good service as well. Recommend!

Delicious, flavorful food -- well-seasoned but not hostile in spice levels, although I suspect if I had said to the nice waitstaff, "EXTRA SPICY, PLEASE?!" they would have complied.  We came in for lunch, had lunch-special portions of dry sauteed string beans, chicken with vegetables, chicken with broccoli, and ma po tofu.  Each dish was a winner: brilliant colors, a lovely balance of seasoning, high-quality ingredients (hey! chicken that tastes like chicken!) -- and a very sweet staff giving splendid service.  The only downside is that if you drive here, bring quarters for the muni-meter and be prepared to leap up every 57 minutes to refill the demanding automaton.  

We'll be back.  Yummy, as we say.

great little spot, very cold weather today so it was nice comfort food. warmed up with some tea right away!

to start we got the bamboo shoots - idk if we're white people who don't know how to order  or we're not used to the spices but it was a miss for me. hot and sour soup was yummy and definitely would get again! regret not getting the tofu and the marinated egg looked interesting but my partner's not as adventurous in food as i am - will have to try in the future!

for mains we got cumin spiced beef (lamb would have been better with the flavors but beef was just my personal preference) and the sweet peanut chicken, which actually complimented each other well! you get steamed rice on the side of course. both really good!! would get again.

we got sweet and spicy pork to go because it was featured in a Tasty video and i was curious... worth it!!! honestly would go back at least once a month for it but it's a far trek.

definitely would come back again!! ideally not when too cold to walk outside. and hopefully i will know which food is actually the best to pick  definitely way better than any random hole in the wall down the street in my area.

Gosh! I love this spot!  This has to be the best Szechuan cuisine in College Point.  They have a red pepper coded menu and it's wise to take it seriously.  For my taste one pepper is  hot and two ... hellfire hot. My fave dishes;  where to start? Spicy Cold Noodles in a rich, fragrant sauce; sliced pork belly in chili-garlic sauce; General Tso's Chicken... and if you're super adventurous, go for the Dried Stir Pig Intestine with hot pepper (real soul food).   They prepare almost every kind of pork, chicken, or rabbit imaginable including stomach, kidney, and other delicacies like Preserved Egg, Surf Clams and Winter Melon.  Takeout is available and they serve alcoholic beverages too. Best of all, their prices are reasonable.

There's metered street parking, but you'll need the ParkNYC app since there aren't many meters that work directly(with coins or credit/debit cards).  

They're closed on Thursdays ... bummer! Check them out people!

A hidden gem in College Point. Whenever I eat here with family, I see a ton of people place huge orders just to do take out. It's authentic; you can tell by the smell of peppers and spices when you walk through their doors. Service is good, host is welcoming, bathroom...could be better.

I loveeee their Dan Dan noodles. They have so many great dishes! I'm not a fan of tofu so I can't say much about it. 

Their spicy fish is SO GOOD. They have cabbage marinating inside the soup, it's so flavorful (but oily). The fish itself wasn't spicy, so make sure to eat it with the soup.

Their mushroom dish is also really good! It's a dry dish. 

Their cabbage dish looks so basic but you need to smell it...it's cooked with pig grease (kind of like bacon oil), and it smells and tastes like heaven. 

I always request for mild spicy and sodium because they're quite heavy handed.

Went for lunch. Very speedy, really good food. Scallion pancake came with amazing dip. The dumplings were excellent, as was the spicy lamb. I think they may have dulled things down for us so if you really want the spice I would make it clear. Nothing too spicy, and the lamb had the "two pepper" icon.

Little Pepper is one of my favorite Sichuan restaurants in NYC. It's not easy to get to if you don't live nearby or have a car, but it's worth it! I love the spicy cumin lamb, the Dan Dan noodles, and the smoked pork and dried mushroom dry pot. If you love spicy food you'll enjoy Little Pepper.

Little Pepper feels like a place that should be in downtown Flushing somewhere, but by being in College Point it serves as easily the neighborhood's default destination for all things Chinese if not Sichuan. Unlike Chinese establishments with their faux/irrelevant English names, Little Pepper is literal with Xiao La Jiao (小辣椒). The food has been consistently tasty and one of the borough's better options for Sichuan style food. 

Something I appreciate about Little Pepper is the fact it's spacious and rarely crowded. I have brought large groups of hungry folks here in the past without reservations and they've been able to accommodate each time. The place is clean and inviting, which I would consider an added bonus. My only hesitation is the men's restroom where there is plenty of room for improvement.

Foodwise, Little Pepper is very good. Classic 川菜 at its best. They make a mean dan dan noodle (擔擔麵), their mapo tofu (麻婆豆腐) has springy bean curd and not too much blackbean in the sauce, their string beans (四季豆) have the perfect crunch to it. While I wish their boiled fish (水煮魚/牛) had more fish and sauce, I am stoked to they have scallion fried rice (蔥油炒飯). In fact, they might be the only ones that have it at this point.

English isn't a strong suit for some of the wait staff, but no matter the menu has pictures of virtually every dish. Service for the most part is good and while the prices are $15+ for many dishes, the quality of the food makes up for it.

I love coming to this authentic Chinese restaurant. When you enter the tables and walls are nicely designed. The tables are distant enough to enjoy dinner with your party . They always have some interesting decor on the walls . 

When you are seated they bring you a nice hot cup of tea  to settle you in . 

Now for the menu , we can only speak about the vegetarian food. I usually go for the scallion rice , dan dan noodles , scallion pie and green beans which are all delicious choices . 

I feel like the experience is always good when your here . I am giving it four stars because I have been here 3 times and they never ever have the garlic water Spinach ! Which I really want to try

The best Dan Dan noodles!
I enjoyed the eggplant and sesame chicken as well!

Satisfied

Little pepper is so soo good. I literally remember coming where every other week. The food is great and the servers are nice. Its a perfect place for an introduction to Szechuan cuisine. I highly recommend coming here if your not familiar with the cuisine. The food is spicy so be prepared.
Love this little restaurant tucked away on College Point Blvd. A must try. The food was really good and your typical Chinese takeout. I also liked the service, Credit Cards accepted.

Regular schezuan food but pretty pricey for us. Things that were a hit for us: beef with scallions, dumplings dipped in sauce. Things that were a miss for us: Dan Dan noodles, scallion fried rice(literally most normal rice ever) and chilly potato(or whatever it's exactly called. They take cards and street parking was ok to find after hours.

Spicy and tongue numbing, that's what I love about Sichuan (aka Szechuan) food.  We stopped by for lunch and had the beef and ox tripe in chile sauce, wonton in hot sauce, wonton in hot & sour sauce, lamb with hot and spicy sauce, and sea bass with hot bean paste.  Everything was done exceptionally well and flavorful.  Reasonably priced, unpretentious with attentive service.  We've never been disappointed with Little Pepper.

Raining Sunday, too lazy to go out. Take out it is! After a quick search we came cross little pepper and from the reviews it looked amazing! 

However that's where the ship quickly sailed. I called in and ordered the braised fish in spicy soup, shredded pork with dry tofu, chilling oil dumpling, and scallion fried rice. 

All the food was not spicy nor numbing. The fish spicy soup base had a slight bitter taste (probably due to the pepper being burnt) with barley any seasoning and the beef tasted gamey.

The fried rice had tons of oil dipping out, and same goes with the shredded pork. 

The only thing that was good was the chill oil dumpling but they poured the chill oil on top of the dumpling and pack it to go, by the time I open it, it was soaked and mushy.

Overall it was a highly fatty meal with so much oil dipping from all the dishes, great if your hang over but not if your looking for a heart attack!

Gotta be all time worst Chinese ever!!  Super SALTY, greasy and over cooked/blackened to the point of being burnt!!! Would have sent it back but wasn't sure if this was normal.  Makes you wonder... why they would serve 'food' like this to their customers...? Don't believe the 4/5 star reviews!

Authentic szechuan at great value point, what else needs to be said?

Okay, a little more will be said. The green beans were both crispy and juicy all at once. The double sauteed fish fillet was my main course, and there were probably over 20 medium sized fish fillet pieces, crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside (crispy and juice seems to be a common theme here). I'm sure Chinese places like this are a dime a dozen in New York City, but even so, I appreciate it very much so.

The food is mediocre.  If you happen to live in the neighborhood, it's an okay option.  But I went out of my way for this so it was a little disappointing.  I really wanted to like this place but it fell short in so many ways. 

The scallion fried rice is interestingly green.  I've never had or heard of this dish before.  There's not much of anything in there. It's also as a tad bit oily and lacks flavor besides tasting salty.  

We also tried the yang zhou fried rice which was much better but nothing special.  It had peas, carrots, roast pork, ham, shrimp, and egg.  Much better tasting than the scallion fried rice but also a little salty.  

The snow pea leaves looked pretty good but was overly salted.  It's like eating a mouthful of salt and using oily salty rice to wash it down.  You get the picture. 

The fish fillet in chili sauce or in chinese "fish cooked in water" was also a let down.  It didn't have enough flavor and wasn't spicy enough.  There's a lot of oil and there usually is but that's all there really was.  

Tried a pork mushroom burdock dish that wasn't supposed to be spicy but was definitely spicy.  So that sucked because it was supposed to be for a toddler.  Nothing special besides being quite salty and oily. 

Overall if you love oily salty not-too-spicy food, this is the place for you!

This restaurant serves some of the best Szechuan food I've ever had! It's Michelin rated and I can definitely tell why. It's kind of hard to find parking in the area but it's definitely worth it to visit this restaurant!

I ordered multiple dishes when I came.
- Starting with the dan dan noodles, it definitely had that Szechuan spice where your tongue feels tingly and the peppercorn flavor feels numbing. It had a bit too much oil in my opinion but I still enjoyed the chewy noodles!
- The sea bass with Chinese pickles was one of my favorite dishes. It was huge and fried perfectly before covered in the sauce. The fish had so much flavor in itself as well. Plus, it's not a spicy dish.
- Another favorite item that took me by surprise was the scallion fried rice. I didn't expect it to be as good as it was. It was so fragrant and flavorful!
- I also enjoyed the lamb with cumin seasonings. The meat was very tender and it wasn't drowned in spices but still had a great kick to it.
- One of the items that I knew I had to get was the Chicken Chongqing style. It was okay. The chicken were in small pieces and fried with peppers. There was so much seasonings all over each piece which seemed a bit too much. 
- The string beans weren't anything special but did give a nice crunchy and kind of refreshing factor to the other dishes that were strong in flavor. 

I'm taking one star off because I was slightly disappointed with the service. It started off well when taking my order but then seemed to go downhill. While wa for the food, I expected to receive the tea for the table but they seemed to forget about my table. I had to get their attention in order to get the tea. I also had to ask twice for iced water because they didn't give it to me the first time I asked. When I ordered a bowl of rice, they gave it to the wrong table and I had to remind them.

Overall, I would still come back because the food was so delicious.

I love Sichuan food and this place always satisfies my cravings for it ! I always get their Dan Dan noodles and spicy fish . It is so good! The service is always great, everyone is very friendly and accommodating.

Wish we could have eaten here, the menu looks delicious. Unfortunately we came in an hour before close and the server stood by our table and stared at us while we were trying to decide what we wanted. We ended up leaving without ordering. If you want to close at 930, close at 930. Very rude and unprofessional.

Great food! Loved the portions definitely a family style restaurant. I came here with my boyfriend on a Friday evening. We ordered a few things and our favorite had to have been the general tso chicken - probably the best I've ever had! The dumplings in the spicy sauce was to die for  point is we can't wait to go back! And you won't either

We order five dishes 

Little spaic 

All test well done 

This place  very clean . Good for parking on the streets 

This place is bigger 

Summer time was very very cooling

Still one of my favorite Szechuan places in the hood. As I've said before, I'm a somewhat newbie when it comes to Szechuan cuisine because I'm not hugely into spicy food / food with too much heat. This place does let you dial it down or add more depending on the dish - very helpful as I'm often eating w/ kids in tow; do mention it to your server. The menu displays little red pepper icons next to the names of half of the dishes so look for the one pepper rating up to a three pepper rating to gauge. Figure mild, medium, and fiery (as per  the server I spoke to). 

Some dishes we ate on this visit (I've enjoyed every visit so just listing based on this one):
- Spicy beef tendon.  Heat was a surprise.  I ate a few pieces before it hit me.  But it was a good surprise even for a simple palate like mine.  Keep the tea cup close.  LOL
- Sauteed String Beans, gotta love that drier texture almost crispy.  So good.  Anything w/ char is good...
- Smoked Tea Duck, great smokiness without overpowering the flavor of the duck.  Moist and fatty...perfect.  So there's not much meat but enough to satisfy the taste buds.  Chew for flavor and discard after.  So juicy.
- Scallion pancakes, gotta try that sauce. I don't know what's in it but it was awesome.  Not your usual soy, this was sweeter but same brown.
- Scallion and Egg Fried rice, as Jando mentioned in his review, this is not made in many establishments so the opportunity lends itself to try it here.  I liked it a lot, just enough of a scallion (green onion) undertone and eggs.  Simple. Just right.
- Always enjoyed the hot chili oil wontons...love that they don't put shrimp in it.  Means I can enjoy it more.  It's a must try.

Note: wait staff is nice and friendly but there could be some language barrier depending on who you get. That's okay because the menu has lots of photos as does Yelp! And each item has a letter/number so you can order by that as well in case.

Canned soda and beers are available. Displayed behind the register counter and some are listed on the menu.

I felt compelled to write this review after eating at a very highly recommended Szechuan place in the Bay Area. Every bite I took, I thought to myself, "Little Pepper is better." In terms of service, there's never a wait (strange given how amazing it is) and the food comes out quickly. The food itself is phenomenal -- fresh, flavorful, and spicy. We usually order 3x as much as we can eat so we have leftovers for a few days. I dream about the scallion fried rice!

My expectations were pretty low when I walked in, but their food is great. Their food isn't just spicy, it's actually tasty. Some places don't balance that well and just overdo it on the spice. Little Pepper balances the flavor very well.
Love this place. Absolutely amazing. Food is great and very clean atmosphere. Staff is very friendly. If you're in the area this Little Pepper is one of the best spots to eat at.

Yep, Szechuan for sure so ask for no spice  for anything mild.

Braised fish in hot oil: fish takes on hotness nicely and is super flaky and filled with wonderful hot pepper spice.

Dan Dan noodles were my least fave. Just a ginger spice that didn't light my fire.

Pork belly appy that keeps the fire going as it is cut like thick bacon, was. not thrilling. Spices bring me back to China. 

Scallion fried rice was good, not overwhelmed like the posts would lead me to believe. Good none the less.

Mao Pu tofu,  is tasty but I can't get past the heavy, hot oil. Not their fault, my own palate. Love it on a hot pot broth. Tofu that doesn't fall apart is key how it was a bit too soft for my liking.

A dedicated Szechuan cooking experience if you enjoy spicy and the hot oil taste.

This is the worst tasting spicy fish in this type of style, it doesn't not taste good at all. The scallions fried rice has a nice flavor however it was a lot too soft and soggy. At last the sweet and spurs pork was terrible. It was soggy and the meat has a porky stinky taste. We can't really eat it. Overall we was excited to try little pepper but very much regret it pretty much want it throw the whole order away.

Dan Dan noodle, scallion fried rice and Mapo tofu are the best plates I usually get. 

The place is nice with cute atmosphere music around,  and workers are not that friendly.

Loved the food here! Stopped by for lunch on Sunday at noon and my husband and I had the place to ourselves, but a lot of people seemed to order takeout. The two men working there were attentive and helpful whenever we needed something. 
We got an assortment of dishes: dan dan noodles, mapo tofu, pork with bean curd, wonton in chili oil, and scallion fried rice. Our favorite dish was the dan dan noodles. It was the most authentic and delicious dan dan noodles we've ever had. The mapo tofu was also another favorite. The numbing sensation it gives and the slightly sour taste went so well with the hot rice. If we had to pick a least favorite dish it would be the wontons. They were seasoned too sweetly for us and the bright pink meat for me personally was off-putting. The pork with bean curd was good but way too salty for us. We barely touched the dish and ended up recooking it at home. Once the saltiness was lessened, we got to enjoy the umami seasoning with numbing spices.  We def want to come back here to try other dishes in the menu.

fish fillet w/ bean curd!
scallion fried rice.

Hot and sour soup was ok.
corn and pine nuts a bit salty.

Great price.
Friendly service.

I am saddened to only give Little Pepper only a 3 rating.  I have been eating at this establishment when it was on Roosevelt Avenue and have been a fan for a long time.  If this review was done last year, it would have been 5 stars.

However, I have noticed a recent general decrease in quality.

For example.

The Beef & Ox Tripe in Chili Sauce, once an amazing go to no doubt appetizer, now often comes out with flavors that are off and also notably has shrunken to half its size in the past year.  

The Dried Sauteed String Bean which tastes great with a touch of char, often comes out tragically burnt.

I've given up trying to make up it's just a bad day excuses for them.

What is the reason for this slippage?  The chef/owner.  Depending on the day, if he is inside actively cooking, the food will be just as good as it was in the past.  

If he is off or outside minding the restaurant, his underlings aren't good, which is a shame.

Please dont go to this restaurant! We ordered the stir fried beef and the meat was spoiled! We told the boss about this issue. He tasted the beef and said it is still good and asked us if we want to take it home. Why would we still want to eat it if he already tried it and didnt taste good. Most importantly, He didnt apologize at all ! 

His attitude was bad and we would not go to this restaurant again!

WORST restaurant I have ever had. Get rid of it please!!
Food was found spoiled and stink. The owner just ignored the complaint and did not apologize. And was told that the food quality varies all the time and is hard to keep it fresh. Hope that Dept of Health  shut this ridiculous restaurant down asap. Extremely bad customer service. It is Evil!

Solid Sichuan food in Whitestone. Away from the madness in downtown flushing so easy to park. Scallion fried rice is also a big hit for the kids. No frills place that can adjust the spice level for individuals.
Great place to eat food is so delicious food is clean and tasty and staff are nice.  I just lkve that restaurant

Value 4/5
Taste 5/5
Service 4/5
Presentation of food 4/5
Appearance of the establishment 4/5

This place is perfect. Finished every single plate! 

Great customer service and great food especially the pork and the fried rice. Only downside was that the Dan Dan noodles were a bit too moist compared to how I'm used to eating them. But it still satisfied my craving. 

Customer service was outstanding, male server was very kind. Got Tsing Tao to accompany the food and it was a perfect pairing. 

Definitely need to come back and try more items on the menu.

Hands down my favorite take out spot in College Point. There's nothing better than sitting in on a Friday night slamming down some mapo tofu and scallion rice. The spicy chicken with peanuts are to die for. If you want something savory, eggplant with garlic won't disappoint. The lunch specials offer a great deal. The wait staff are always very friendly when I go there to pick up. My next goal is to have a sit down dinner and try their fish.. it looks incredible. I've ordered take out here at least 10 times.. and I usually don't like to go to the same place because I love trying new things. This is a college point classic!

I fell in love with Szechuan food a few years ago. I believe Spy-C in Forest Hills really got me hooked. Since then I've tried a bunch of Szechuan places (Szechuan mountain house, Han Dynasty, Guan Fu) and really love Little Pepper a lot. I love that it's not all hyped up and super chill. I love the prices. Parking isn't too bad around here at all. The food is delicious. I've been here twice. Most recently I tried the braised fish in picked vegetable sauce/broth and LOVED the flavor in it, particularly in the pickled vegetables. I also ordered snow pea leafs (for $12!) and they were so refreshing while I ate the slightly spicy dan dan noodles (not as spicy as Han Dynasty or Guan Fu but spicier than Spy-C for those who have been to all these places). I'll be back again for sure!

This place is amazing!  Really a gem.  Food is fantastic and family opened and run. Feel and taste the love.  And see it too the art on the wall is made by the husband of the owner. He's also the pastry chef.  And the desserts are LEGIT!!!!

Ordered from here on Christmas Day

Pros:
- Food was great and spicy!
- Good prices 

Cons:
- The portion sizes for the meat entrees was on the smaller end
- Food took a while to prepare - waited an extra 10-15 minutes on top of their expected pick up time

Living on Long Island has its good and bad but the absolute worst is great Chinese food. I had this place bookmarked for a while and since traffic is light on January1 we decided to try it. This place will not disappoint you. The food is excellent the staff is very nice and we all loved everything we ate. Finally Chinese food with flavor and spice. Where else can you sit next to a Chinese man wearing a yarmulke eating only vegetarian dishes because he keeps kosher. (Only in NY)
The best part is they just started making homemade desserts by the owner son in law who used to work for a place in the city I forget the name. The desserts were delicious and very inexpensive.

Wow, only gotten delivery from this place and it was honestly soo delicious. Have seen the green fried rice many times on food baby/other food instagrams and have been dying to try, but unfortunately inconvenient to get to via public transportation. 

Ordered from here for Chinese New Year and was not disappointed. Double cooked pork belly was decadent and fatty, without being nauseating. Pieces of crunchy cabbage were a nice touch to break up the oil. Beef with scallion was so tender and juicy, sauce was deliciously savory and umami. Dry cooked cabbage was relatively more plain but still tasty all the same. The scallion fried rice was awesome. So unique, not sure how they get it so green like that? 

Worth the hype!
The green onion fried rice is the bomb! But I always love everything here. Go to place sometimes with my coworkers for lunch!

Heard (more like saw) about this place through foodbaby and immediately wanted to try it. Came here with my husband and we ordered the mapo tofu, scallion fried rice, dan dan noodles, dumpling in hot sauce, chicken in chonquing style. It was definitely wayy too much food for two people but what can I say...we were overwhelmed and wanted to try everything. And it did not disappoint. Everything was delicious and spicy goodness. Service was also very fast and efficient. Plenty of street parking...or at least the times we've been there. Highly recommend this place if you're up for some heat!

Just ordered via Uber eats during the corona pandemic, food was great, not too heavy or greasy, in fact it was quite healthy for general tsos chicken, super fresh and the portion was just right

God bless you guys

Order some delivery through ubereats during this pandemic. Not sure if they are running low on product or not, but the portion sizes are much smaller than they usually are. I'm talking about really small, like it barely took up a quarter of the space in the container. The food was good though, just wish that there would have been more.

I order uber eats takeout for my family in Queens remotely from Little Pepper. They told me the food was tasty.

Pros: Open during COVID
Offering most of their menu items, and they have a huge menu
Food is very authentic

Cons: Prices were noticeably inflated on Uber eats versus their pre covid prices on their menu. See this doesnt bother me if it's off by $1 because I know using Uber eats is expensive for the restaurant...but it was a lot more than that. Each dish was 3 dollars more expensive, which at the price point of this chinese restaurant, makes it 20-25% more expensive per dish... 

Oh well, I can give them the benefit of the doubt that maybe costs for the has risen due to the pandemic. Still worth ordering from during this time.

we were v excited to try this out, but food was just okay compared to the other nearby sichuan restaurants. there's just a few places that make scallion fried rice and theirs was so on the greasier side.

A taste of Szechuan heaven!  We missed Little Pepper so much. They offered delivery , but we live too far. Today when I called, their message changed; they started taking curbside orders via their Facebook page. Hallelujah!  These are our go to, must eat dishes; chicken Chongqing style (if u like fried food,) chicken w/ peanut in hot pepper sauce, lamb in hot and spicy sauce with cumin, shredded pork with bamboo shoots & Theo amazing braised fish in spicy soup base (I take the spicy broth home and make a meal with it; I add veggies, noodle and poached egg.  I'm so glad to taste your wonderfulness again. We'll in back.
Love the food at this place - best takeout in the area!. Something for everyone from mild to spicy  dishes.

Little pepper is NO joke. They are bringing heat and flavor in every bite. They are doing take out and deliver right now!
Would order again:
- scallion fried rice
- beef with scallions
- Dan Dan noodles (hot!!)
- chicken congqin

We order delivery to Elmhurst from here all the time.  It is admittedly very spicy, so if you cannot handle spicy food, I would be careful ordering them here.  It is extremely enjoyable and delicious, specifically the FuQi Fei Pian, the Mapo Tofu, the Fish in Chili sauce, Dan Dan Mian (spiciest Dan Dan mian we've ever had and it's great!), and the general Tso's chicken.  Whenever we are bored, we order something different from here and it has been delicious everytime.
Not bad. I'm always looking for good Mapo Tofu places. I like SPICY food, but the Mapo Tofu from here wasn't that spicy.
Drove from Greenpoint to try this place and was totally worth it. I usually go to birds of a feather for Sichuan food but this is better.
This is my go to pace when I want some spicy food. I highly recommend it. I haven't had had a bad dish yet. Love this place

Little Pepper you are absolutely incredible, I had a lovely experience here today. It's in a perfect location and we were definitely pleased with our experience. Little Pepper has an outstanding P19 Sichuan Style Double Cooked Pork, give it a try I think you would really like it, I certainly love it. Service was fabulous and every one working here was extremely nice and hospitable. Little Pepper... What a great find.
I really liked their scallion fried rice. I also got their home style tofu but it was bland. Garlic chicken was good and wontons was mediocre.
This is my absolutely fav spot for Sichuan food.  They are the nicest people - small and family run - the food here is beyond outstanding.

Went back after my 1 star review of this place a few years back and now I'm 1000000% positive the negative reviews is still correct as it stands. I placed my order thru Facebook as they current DO NOT take phone calls atm, my order time was 6:17pm for 6 dishes total including sides dishes that are premade 2, time estimated 7:00pm pick up. I arrive at 7:18pm and the lady informs me SOON, so OK I ask how long more I'll wait in my car. After 15 more minutes I go in and ask again and then she tells me honestly my chef hasn't started cooking your order yet. She then tells me 40 minutes more before its finally ready and currently she hires 1 chef in the back so wait..... so don't lie about it!!!!

Food is ok for Szechuan. Nothing special compared to other Szechuan restaurants that know what they are doing. Their problem is that they think they are special. They won't even take orders over the phone. You need to order through Instagram or Uber eats. On top of that, if you finally get through to them, they just hang up on you if you ask two questions. Next time I will make sure we only ask one question, oh wait...I will never order from them again.

My favorite restaurant in NYC, Sichuan or not. Amazing food at good prices, and just really tasty and varied Sichuan food overall-- best Dan Dan noodles I've had yet, and you almost want to bottle the broth the sesame cold noodles comes in. I've been here countless times with my gf, and it's way better than Famous Sichuan and Spicy Village, better than Legend of Taste, Grain House, Sichuan Mountain House, it edges ahead of Mala Project... and blows Han Dyansty out of the water. Great food, good people, and quirky art on the wall! Love this place!

We eat at a lot of Szechuan restaurants in NYC but Little Pepper is definitely our favorite. It is worth the trek from Brooklyn to Flushing for this food. It's routine to order a few days worth of food each time lol. Fish braised in hot oil, dumplings, Dan Dan noodles, Chongqing chicken. We always order the cumin chicken. This is off menu but they have been making it for us for many years. The little pepper fried rice is also a must try!
Literally one of the best restaurants in queens. Amazing service and delicious food and owned by one of the nicest families.
Good spot. Must order the following: Scallion fried rice. Chicken in cold chili oil app. Make sure you get your free tea for dine in and grab a water while you're at it, you'll need it

This is a pretty plain looking restaurant but do not be deceived, they serve authentic and delicious Chinese food. 

You must order scallion rice - it's sooo good! What could be in it? MSG probable, we kid. Seriously, it was so flavorful. 

I also enjoyed the sweet chicken dish and had the leftovers the next day.

The food was delicious.  I ordered shredded pork and garlic sauce and general Taos chicken and the were very tasty but hot hot hot.  The scallion rice was really good.  I went on a Sunday afternoon and it was pleasantly quiet.  I may make this a regular after church spot since I know of the slow time.  Two friends with me loved it all.  I can't  wait to try other dishes.  The service was speedy and accommodating.

i'm not an expert but this is the best szechuan food i've had in NYC. really quality, nice service. we did the dan dan noodles and the dry pot green beans (A+++) and the cumin lamb and the kung pao chicken. all very good.
Food is amazing and never disappoints. My go to spot when I crave authentic Chinese food
Its the best. They don't miss. You can throw a dart at the menu and you'll get something delicious guaranteed

This Chinese restaurant has really good food. There should be more selections on the menu but all in all it's very tasty especially if you like a little spice.! When we arrived there, we were the only couple there, which is very unusual for this place . Why I'm giving it 4 stars instead of 5 is because they sat two couples right next to us, and they were loud, laughing and drinking when there was  20 tables empty it ruined my dining experience, but we enjoyed the food! Also, they charged four dollars for two small bowls of white rice. I find that ridiculous.!

I've eaten at a lot of Szechuan places, and this is by far the best one I've been to. This is mainly due to their huge selection of dishes, many of which I've never heard of, and the fact that they actually cater to a wide variety of palates and spice tolerances. 

Items I would get again, ranked by preference, were the thinly sliced pork belly, sautéed cabbage, chicken in garlic sauce, beef and ox tripe, scallion fried rice, and preserved egg. All these dishes were packed with flavor. I loved how thin the pork belly was, and the cabbage was a really nice palate cleanser from all the oily/fried items since it wasn't salty. 

The two items I would pass on next time are the dumplings in hot sauce and the chongqing chicken. Even despite that, both were also really good. The dumplings just felt a little basic to me and the chicken was too tough for my liking. Honestly though it seems like you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. 

We came on a Saturday around 7pm and only a couple of tables were occupied. The food came out quickly and service was great. I really wish I lived closer because I already want to come back!

Best Szechuan hands down I've ever had!!  How this place doesn't have Michelin stars is beyond me. I absolutely love their food. Highly recommend their beef and scallion along with their scallion rice. Great service! Quick and delicious food!

I got the scallion fried rice, beef with scallion, and the Dan Dan noodles for takeout. I thought the beef with scallion was really good and tender. The Dan Dan noodles were decent, thought it could be spicier but it was a little salty. The scallion fried rice though just tasted like regular fried rice and nothing to rave about. I was excited to try the fried rice especially with all the reviews raving about it but really could not find anything special about it. It was also super expensive. It was 44 dollars for these 3 dishes.

The best szechuan in flushing/college point. Made with care, fresh ingredients, clean, and great family run business. Highly recommend. Pick up or eat in so all funds go to the restaurant. 

 1) cumin lamb
 2) shredded pork with bean curd  
 3) shredded pork with bamboo shoot 
 4) fish filet with pickled cabbage soup 
 5) mapo tofu
Very good Szechuan food in college point. Scallion fried was delicious! Every dish was so flavorful! I enjoyed the restaurant! It's a must go if you're into Szechuan mala flavors!
Really good food. Favorites are scallion rice, dried string beans and home style tofu. Great friendly service.
Despite some Yelper reporting this establishment is closed that is not true! Check their Instagram for updates! littlepeppernyc

Please continue to support little pepper as it's not closed permanently or temporarily 

Go and support
Best food in queens, HANDS DOWN! Delicious, spicy, flavorful, fresh, makes you wanting more!

The moment that we sat down we were greeted by the owner. The menu was filled with authentic Chinese dishes The hostess who I believe was the owner helped us choose appetizers which were delicious. We picked entrees and they came out piping hot and fresh in decent timing.

This place is so good and definitely one of the best Chinese food establishments in Queens. It is out of the way for sure, but I would say it's worth it for the food! The pork and bean curd, scallion fried rice, mapo tofu, string bean, and intestines in soup base are all delicious.

If there's one thing they're known for, it's the scallion fried rice so definitely give it a try! It's so addicting... 

I've ordered from Little Pepper about ten times, and they have never missed the mark. The staff are also super kind (if you speak Chinese).

The owner here is really sweet and is planning to retire soon, so come here before it changes ownership. The food was good. The scallion fried rice is definitely unique and pretty good but not as a stand alone dish. It's more of a side dish to eat the other food with. I really enjoyed the lamb with onions and scallions. Very tasty and not spicy. We also had mapo tofu but I wasn't a fan. Maybe because we asked for mild and no pork.

Sweet couple running the spot. Husband I assume cooks and wife takes orders. My friend and I enjoyed the food. The commute here is brutal. But nice spot. 

There was no one there when we went. Super quiet and chill spot.

Little Pepper is the best authentic Sichuan restaurant in New York City! Their menu has savory, scrumptious, and spicy specialties and delicacies from Sichuan Province. Every dish is cooked to perfection. Allow yourself and guests to an amazing epicurean journey to Sichuan at Little Pepper! Exceptional food and service! You will love this place and keep coming back - simply delicious!

Might be the best Chinese food I ever had. Service was non existent but lady was really nice but honestly with food this good who cares? I love this place can't wait to go back. Place was not crowded at all I hope it stays that way.

My daughter and I were headed to the nearby airport to pick up the rest of the family and we wanted something good to eat on the way. Found Little Pepper and knew it was the answer. Much easier to access than the Flushing spots but it absolutely stands up to them.

Seating is comfortable and the restaurant is quiet enough for a conversation. Certainly seemed to be a family operation. Very nice woman working the front of house and a gentleman preparing all of the dishes. It felt like dining at someone's house, they served a table at a time. If you were late to a nearby theater, this may not be the choice for you. If you're patient and looking to eat an authentic meal, this is the place!

At the tail end of a hard eating weekend, we didn't want to order too much. We checked out the menu while enjoying a complimentary pot of tasty tea. (Hint of oolong) We ordered silken tofu with scallion sauce, cumin lamb, sesame chicken, and pork fried rice. Menu had at least 30 items I would like to try. Silken tofu and cumin lamb packed flavor and a solid spice level. Probably not their spiciest dishes but they delivered. Lamb was tender and the tofu was in fact "silken". My daughter's sesame chicken was a high end example of a basic dish. The pork fried rice delivered quality ingredients made in a non salty/greasy way.

Excellent dinner!
Gorgeous! authentic Sichuan dishes. Good staff at the restaurant. You don't want to miss this place.

Small mom & pop establishment that puts out delicious Szechuan home cooked dishes. Our go-to dishes include eggplant and chicken in garlic sauce, bamboo shoots & pork, dan dan noodles, dumplings in hot oil etc.

This restaurant hs been in the same location on College Point Blvd for many years. The prices are reasonable however the food sometimes takes a long time.  It's literally a 2 person operation.  Mom serves the food upfront and pops cooks in the kitchen. I highly recommend Little Pepper if you like spicy szechuan!

Street parking is available. The neighborhood looks sketchy but is OK during the day.

This bad experience just made me a terrible ending for my traveling in NYC. It seems like a family running Chinese restaurant but bad service ever. Yes, money is probably the best and only thing we the people care about.
Been coming to this place for a decade, one of my favorite authentic spicy spot  local family owned, boss lady is the most friendly and heart warming

Absolutely amazing Szechuan restaurant. Everything is fresh and made to order. As others have mentioned, it's run by the sweetest family. The ambience is great and family-friendly. Highly recommend coming here while still under the original ownership.

They claimed themselves Szechuan. I am the spicy queen and I am a big fan of Szechuan food. I have eaten all amazing authentic Szechuan food in Flushing. Those are so good. One night I and my family were just hungry and wanted to eat something. I assume the wife is the server and the husband is the cook. They are very sweet. They have nice service however we need to wait the food for a long time to cook. The Chongqing chicken is so oily and just salty. It doesn't taste burning sensation of something. When I eat the dried chillies, the chillies are just oily and no taste while other restaurants' chillies in their Chongqing chicken are so tasty. Just the chillies but very tasty. This one is no. They have no taste. The chicken is not crispy at all just oily and salty on the outside. We also ordered cumin lamb. The cumin lamb is just salty and still stinky. While other restaurants' cumin lamb is not stinky and very Szechuan taste with burning and spicy sensation and the cumin fragrance in your throat. We ordered the beef lomein, its not bad. Its edible. The white pepper is strong, so if you like this kind of taste. This is good place for you. If you are just hungry and want to order asian food quickly, this is the place. If you want to have yummy and genuine Szechuan taste food, I don't think this is the place. The place of the restaurant is really nice. The vibe is nice. The bathroom is clean. The server is warm and nice.

There is one reason to go to this place, and it's for the scallion fried rice. That's it! It's so damn good! Everything else is good as well, but I would die for that green rice. It's a sweet little restaurant run by a lovely married couple, so go ahead and support this small business. There are paintings everywhere in the restaurant, and the lady who runs it is super sweet.
